o: The petition must fail, since only a person whose own legal right is harmed by the appointment may seek a writ against it.
Mandamus is the proper writ, directing the state government to cancel the appointment and appoint a citizen instead.
Quo warranto lies, but the appointment survives, since an OCI cardholder has parity with NRIs in practising as an advocate.
Quo warranto lies at the advocate's instance, since the office is open only to citizens and standing is relaxed for it.
qs.e: Quo warranto asks by what authority a person holds a public office, and any public-spirited person may seek it, so the lack of a personal stake is no bar. The office of Advocate General is open only to citizens; a person who took foreign citizenship is a foreign national, and an OCI card gives no right to hold public office. The NRI- parity option tempts because cardholders may practise law, but practising is not holding the office. Mandamus orders a duty to be done; it does not oust a usurper. Remember: quo warranto tests the holder's title, and anyone may ask.

qs.q:
With reference to testing the fast track created by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019 against the guarantee of equality, consider the following statements:
1. Article 14 is available to all persons, so migrants left outside the fast track can invoke it.
2. Such migrants can also invoke the bar in Article 15(1) on discrimination on grounds of religion.
3. The 2019 Act cuts the aggregate period of residence or service needed for naturalisation from eleven years to five for migrants of six faiths from three neighbouring countries.
4. Under Article 14, the question is whether the classification rests on an intelligible differentia that has a rational nexus with the object of the law.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Article 14 protects every person, so a migrant left outside the fast track, which cuts the naturalisation period from eleven years to five, can invoke it, and the court will ask whether the classification rests on an intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the law's object. Statement 2 fails because Article 15, with its bar on religious discrimination, protects citizens alone. It tempts because a religion- based classification makes Article 15 look like the natural ground. Remember: the CAA debate runs through Article 14, not Article 15.

qs.q:
Life insurance, fourteen major banks and general insurance were nationalised, and the privy purses of former rulers were ended. These steps were defended under Articles 38 and 39, and they led to long court battles over property. Consider the following statements:
1. Directive Principles were used to justify economic measures that cut into private property.
2. If such a step were taken today, the owner could not move the Supreme Court under Article 32 for the loss of property as such, since property is now a legal right under Article 300A.
3. Because Articles 38 and 39 cannot be enforced in court, laws made to carry them out could not be challenged in court at all.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. These steps were defended under Articles 38 and 39 and cut into private property. Property is now a legal right under Article 300A, outside Part III, so its loss as such cannot go to the Supreme Court under Article 32; the route is Article 226. Statement 3 fails because a law made to carry out a Directive is still open to challenge for breaching a Fundamental Right; it tempts by treating an unenforceable goal as an unchallengeable law. Remember: a Directive cannot be enforced, but a law made under it can be challenged.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about a "religious denomination" under Article 26 is correct?
o: It must form a religious minority in the state in which it claims the right.
Any trust registered for a religious purpose counts as a denomination.
Both the Aurobindo Society and Ananda Marga have been held to qualify.
It needs a common faith, a common organisation and a distinctive name.
qs.e: A religious denomination under Article 26 is a group with a common faith, a common organisation and a distinctive name. On that test the Ramakrishna Mission and Ananda Marga qualify, but the Aurobindo Society does not, which is why the option pairing it with Ananda Marga fails. Minority status matters under Article 30, not Article 26, and a trust registered for a religious purpose is not a denomination merely by being registered. The minority option tempts because minority rights sit close by in Part III. Remember: faith, organisation and name make a denomination.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax:
1. It came into force on 1 July 2017 through the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016.
2. It is a destination-based tax on the supply of goods and services, charged at each stage with credit for the tax paid on inputs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Both statements are correct. GST began on 1 July 2017 under the Constitution (101st Amendment) Act, 2016, and it is a destination-based, multi-stage tax on the supply of goods and services, with credit for tax paid on inputs, so each stage pays only on the value it adds. Neither statement changes a date, an Article or the tax base. A doubt may arise because Budget changes usually start in April, but GST started in July. Remember: GST, 1 July 2017, 101st Amendment, tax goes to the place of consumption.

qs.q: Under the ceiling set by the Sixteenth Finance Commission for 2026-31, a State has a GSDP of Rs 10 lakh crore. In one year its fiscal deficit is Rs 34,000 crore, of which Rs 6,000 crore is borrowing under the Special Assistance Scheme for Capital Investment, which is not counted against the ceiling. Taking the ceiling as 3 per cent of GSDP, by how much could the State borrow further in that year without crossing the ceiling?
qs.e: The answer is Rs 2,000 crore. The ceiling is 3 per cent of GSDP, 0.03 multiplied by 10,00,000 crore, which is Rs 30,000 crore. Loans under the capital-investment scheme are not counted, so the deficit measured against the ceiling is 34,000 minus 6,000, which is Rs 28,000 crore, leaving 30,000 minus 28,000 as room. Rs 4,000 crore comes from comparing the full deficit with the ceiling, and Rs 6,000 crore is only the excluded loan. Remember: ceiling minus (deficit less capital-investment loans).

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of taxes in India:
1. The fringe benefit tax was classed as a direct tax.
2. The interest tax was classed as a direct tax.
3. The Securities Transaction Tax is an indirect tax, because it is charged when a trade takes place.
4. Wealth tax, now abolished, was also a direct tax.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Three statements are correct. The fringe benefit tax, the interest tax and wealth tax were all direct taxes, and so is the Securities Transaction Tax. Statement 3 fails on its conclusion: the Securities Transaction Tax is a direct tax, even though it is levied when a trade takes place, because the burden stays with the person taxed. The trade-based charge tempts because it looks like a tax on a transaction, which is the mark of an indirect tax. Remember: STT is charged on a trade but classed as direct.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a feature and the legal position on black money and benami property:
1. Benami property : Held in another person's name and open to confiscation under the Act of 1988 as amended in 2016
2. A transaction whose owner is unaware of it : Ceases to be benami for that reason
3. Appellate Tribunal : Provided by the benami law, together with investigating and adjudicating authorities
4. Black Money Act on undisclosed foreign income and assets : Taxes undisclosed foreign assets
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched. Benami property, held in another's name, can be confiscated under the Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act, 1988 as amended in 2016; the Act provides an Appellate Tribunal with investigating and adjudicating authorities; and the Black Money Act taxes undisclosed foreign assets. Pair 2 reverses the rule: a transaction stays benami even when the owner is unaware of it. Lack of knowledge tempts as a defence. Remember: ignorance of the owner does not cure a benami transaction.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the sharing of Union taxes with the States, as the rules stood in the year 2000:
1. Until the Constitution (80th Amendment) Act, 2000, corporation tax was kept wholly by the Union.
2. The 80th Amendment widened Article 270 so that Union taxes and duties in general are shared with the States.
3. The Tenth Commission's award, in force from 1 April 1995, shared corporation tax together with income tax and Union excise duties.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Corporation tax stayed wholly with the Union until the Constitution (80th Amendment) Act, 2000, which widened Article 270 so that Union taxes and duties in general are shared. Statement 3 adds corporation tax to the Tenth Commission's award from 1 April 1995, which shared only income tax and Union excise duties. It tempts because the pool now covers corporation tax. Remember: 1995 award, income tax and excise; 2000 amendment, everything.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Thirteenth Finance Commission:
1. It proposed a plan for creating lakhs of jobs.
2. It proposed a design for the Goods and Services Tax, with a compensation package linked to adherence to that design.
3. It recommended grants to local bodies as a specified share of the central divisible pool.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Thirteenth Commission proposed a design for GST with a compensation package linked to adherence to that design, and recommended grants to local bodies as a specified share of the central divisible pool. Statement 1 is wrong because it proposed no plan for lakhs of jobs; that belongs to employment programmes, not to a Finance Commission award. The job plan tempts because it sounds like a development goal. Remember: Thirteenth, GST design plus local-body share.

qs.q: Under the rules for transfers on or after 23 July 2024, an investor sells listed shares on which Securities Transaction Tax is paid. The shares sold after 14 months give a gain of Rs 1,50,000, and other listed shares sold after 8 months give a gain of Rs 2,00,000. There are no other gains in the year. Ignoring surcharge and cess, what is the total tax on the two gains?
qs.e: The tax is Rs 43,125. The 14-month gain is long term: (1,50,000 minus 1,25,000) at 12.5 per cent is Rs 3,125. The 8-month gain is short term at 20 per cent: 2,00,000 at 20 per cent is Rs 40,000. The total is Rs 43,125. Rs 58,750 forgets the Rs 1.25 lakh exemption, Rs 33,125 uses the old 15 per cent short-term rate, and Rs 70,000 taxes all gains at 20 per cent. Remember: 20 per cent short; 12.5 per cent long above Rs 1.25 lakh.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Centre's tax revenue:
Statement I: The share of Union excise duty in gross tax revenue has become smaller since GST began.
Statement II: GST absorbed most goods and every service, so Union excise was left chiefly with petroleum and tobacco.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. Once GST took over most goods and all services, Union excise was left mainly on petroleum and tobacco, so it makes up a smaller share of gross tax revenue. Nothing in either statement is changed. The explanation may be doubted because excise on petroleum is still large, but the share of the whole has still fallen, since the base shrank. Remember: GST took the base, excise kept petroleum and tobacco.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about black money:
Statement I: The main worry black money causes the Government is the loss of revenue to the exchequer.
Statement II: Black money arises from illegal underreporting or concealment of income, which keeps back tax that should have been paid.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. Tax evasion, the illegal underreporting or concealment of income, keeps tax from reaching the Treasury, and that loss of revenue to the exchequer is the Government's main worry about black money. Neither statement alters a fact. A reader may think Statement II merely restates the topic, but it names the cause of the loss. Remember: concealed income, tax unpaid, revenue lost.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about tax buoyancy:
1. It measures how revenue responds when the tax rate itself is changed.
2. A value above one means that tax revenue is growing faster than the economy, which can happen even without a rise in rates.
3. If tax revenue grows 12 per cent while nominal GDP grows 10 per cent, buoyancy is 1.2.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Buoyancy is the per cent change in tax revenue divided by the per cent change in GDP, so a value above one means revenue outgrows the economy, which can happen with no new rate, and 12 divided by 10 is 1.2. Statement 1 describes tax elasticity, which asks how revenue responds to a change in the rate itself. It tempts because the two ideas are close. Remember: buoyancy follows GDP; elasticity follows the rate.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about the sector-specific grants of the Fifteenth and the Sixteenth Finance Commissions is correct?
o: The Sixteenth Commission set aside Rs 45,000 crore as an incentive for States carrying out agricultural reforms.
The Fifteenth Commission recommended no sector-specific grants and left school education wholly to the States.
Both Commissions recommended Rs 4,800 crore for better school education outcomes between 2022-23 and 2025-26 as a performance-linked grant.
The Fifteenth Commission kept Rs 45,000 crore for States doing agricultural reforms, while the Sixteenth recommended none.
qs.e: The fourth statement is correct. The Fifteenth Commission recommended Rs 4,800 crore for 2022-23 to 2025-26 for better school education outcomes and kept Rs 45,000 crore as a performance incentive for agricultural reforms; the Sixteenth recommended no sector-specific grants. The first option gives the Rs 45,000 crore to the Sixteenth, the second denies the Fifteenth any such grant, and the third credits the Rs 4,800 crore to both. Remember: sector grants belong to the Fifteenth, none to the Sixteenth.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the criteria used to divide the States' share of the divisible pool:
1. Income distance asks how poor a State is, and it measures the gap from the average income of the three highest-income large States.
2. Forest and ecology asks which States protect forests at a cost to their own revenue.
3. Area asks which States brought down population growth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Income distance measures the gap between a State's per capita income and the average of the three highest-income large States, so poorer States gain, and forest and ecology rewards States that protect forests at a cost to their own revenue. Statement 3 gives the question of demographic performance to area, whose question is how large a territory must be covered. The swap tempts because both are listed together. Remember: area is territory; demographic performance is slowed growth.

qs.q: Which one of the following was among the proposals of the Kelkar Task Force on direct taxes of 2002?
o: A higher exemption limit for widows, along with abolition of wealth tax
Retention of wealth tax, along with exemption of dividends from tax
A larger standard deduction, along with exemption of long-term gains on listed equity held for more than one year
Removal of the standard deduction, with exemption of dividends and long-term gains on listed equity
qs.e: The last option is correct. The Kelkar Task Force of 2002 proposed abolishing wealth tax, removing the standard deduction, and exempting dividends and long-term gains on listed equity. It did not propose a higher exemption limit for widows, which spoils the first option. The second keeps wealth tax and the third enlarges the standard deduction, both the reverse of what was proposed. The widows' limit tempts as a plausible relief. Remember: Kelkar removed wealth tax and the standard deduction.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about the Fourteenth Finance Commission is correct?
o: It was chaired by N. K. Singh, covered the years 2021-26 and set the share at 41 per cent.
It left the States with 41 per cent of the divisible pool because Ladakh was carved out.
It made recommendations on sector-specific grants as well as on the States' share of the pool.
It was chaired by Y. V. Reddy and raised the States' share from 32 to 42 per cent.
qs.e: The fourth statement is correct. The Fourteenth Commission, chaired by Y. V. Reddy, covered 2015-16 to 2019-20 and raised the States' share of the divisible pool from 32 to 42 per cent, a rise of 10 percentage points; it made no recommendation on sector-specific grants. N. K. Singh chaired the Fifteenth, which covered 2021-26 and put the share at 41 per cent. Remember: Reddy, 32 to 42; Singh, 41.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fifteenth Finance Commission's criteria for dividing the States' share:
1. Governance reforms and stable government were among its criteria.
2. It brought back a tax and fiscal effort criterion with a weight of 2.5.
3. Contribution to GDP carried a weight of 10 among its criteria.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only one statement is correct: the second. The Fifteenth Commission, besides population, area and income distance, used demographic performance, forest and ecology, and tax and fiscal effort, the last with a weight of 2.5. Statement 1 names criteria that were never used. Statement 3 borrows from the Sixteenth Commission, which gave contribution to GDP a weight of 10 while dropping tax effort. Remember: the Fifteenth had tax effort, the Sixteenth has contribution to GDP.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a feature of the GST Council and its rule:
1. Quorum of the Council : Half of its members
2. Recommendations of the Council : Binding on the Union and on every State
3. Votes held by all States together : Two-thirds
4. Majority needed for a decision : Three-fourths of the votes of members present and voting
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Pairs 1, 3 and 4 are correctly matched. The quorum is half of the members, the States together hold two-thirds of the votes against the Union's one-third, and a decision needs three-fourths of the votes of members present and voting. Pair 2 fails because the Council's recommendations are not binding on the Union or the States, and Parliament and the State legislatures can act on their own. A joint forum with such a high majority tempts a belief that it binds. Remember: three-fourths to decide, yet not binding.

qs.q:
The figure given below shows the new-regime slab staircase for income of 2025-26. Consider the following statements:
Statement I: A person with taxable income of Rs 15 lakh has slab tax of Rs 1,05,000 before cess, which is Rs 60,000 on the first Rs 12 lakh plus 15 per cent of the remaining Rs 3 lakh.
Statement II: This is because, once income passes Rs 12 lakh, the 15 per cent rate is applied to the person's entire income.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct and Statement II is not. Read band by band, Rs 4 lakh to Rs 8 lakh gives 5 per cent and Rs 8 lakh to Rs 12 lakh gives 10 per cent, which is Rs 60,000, and the extra Rs 3 lakh at 15 per cent is Rs 45,000, a total of Rs 1,05,000. Statement II fails because slabs are marginal: only income inside a band meets its rate. The top step tempts as a rate on everything. Remember: a step taxes the slice, not the whole income.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a tax and its classification:
1. Income tax : Direct tax, because the burden stays with the person taxed
2. GST : Indirect tax, because it is collected from one person and borne by another
3. Corporation tax : Indirect tax, because the company can pass it on to buyers
4. Union excise duty : Direct tax, because the manufacturer pays it to the Government
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. Income tax is direct because impact and incidence fall on one person, and GST is indirect because the seller collects it and the buyer bears it. Corporation tax is also direct, not indirect, and Union excise duty is indirect even though the manufacturer is the person who pays it over; who hands over the money does not decide the class. Remember: direct means the burden cannot be shifted.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. A State finds that its own taxes fall short of its spending on health, police and farms. Money from the Union reaches it by three kinds of channel: a share of Union taxes that the Union levies and collects, grants-in-aid, and loans. A grant may be made for a public purpose even where the matter lies outside the legislative field of the government making it. A State may borrow within India on the security of its Consolidated Fund within limits set by law. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The sharing of Union taxes rests on Article 270, while grants-in-aid rest on Articles 275 and 282.
2. A grant for a public purpose may be made only on a matter inside the legislative field of the government making it.
3. The borrowing of a State within India rests on Article 293.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Conclusions 1 and 3 are correct. The share of Union taxes rests on Article 270, grants-in-aid on Articles 275 and 282, and loans on Article 293. Conclusion 2 reverses the passage, which says a grant for a public purpose may be made even where the matter lies outside the granting government's legislative field; this is the reach of Article 282. It tempts because spending normally follows a government's own field. Remember: 270 share, 275 and 282 grants, 293 loans.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about a tax and a fee:
1. A tax is a voluntary payment to the Government that is not tied to a specific service.
2. A fee, unlike a tax, buys one particular service.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. A tax is a compulsory payment to the Government with no specific service in return, whereas a fee buys one particular service. Statement 1 fails on the word voluntary: nobody may opt out of a tax, though they do not receive a particular service for it. The word tempts because the second half of the sentence is true as printed. Remember: a tax is compulsory and untied; a fee is paid for one service.

qs.q:
The figure given below shows the States' share of the divisible pool under four Commissions, the last for 2026-31. Consider the following statements:
1. Between the Thirteenth and the Fourteenth awards the share rose by 10 percentage points.
2. The Fifteenth award stands 1 percentage point below the Fourteenth.
3. By the Sixteenth award, for 2026-31, the share has fallen by 2 percentage points from the Fourteenth.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The share went from 32 to 42 per cent, a rise of 10 percentage points, and then to 41 per cent in the Fifteenth award, a fall of 1 percentage point because Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory and Ladakh was carved out. Statement 3 fails on the number: the Sixteenth award kept 41 per cent, so the fall from the Fourteenth stays 1 point. The 2 tempts as a second step down. Remember: 32, 42, 41, 41.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about agricultural income and the Union's power to tax:
1. The Union can tax agricultural income as such, because the Income-tax Act is a law of Parliament.
2. Selling rural agricultural land gives a capital gain.
3. Income from poultry farming and wool rearing is not exempt as agricultural income.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only one statement is correct: the third. Income from poultry farming and wool rearing is not exempt as agricultural income. Statement 1 fails because the Seventh Schedule leaves agricultural income to the States, so the Union cannot tax it. Statement 2 fails because rural agricultural land is not a capital asset, so its sale gives no capital gain. Many assume the opposite pair, that land gives a gain and poultry income is exempt. Remember: land, no gain; poultry and wool, not exempt.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about taxes on stock-exchange and futures-market transactions, other than stamp duties:
1. They fall in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule.
2. The Union levies them, but the States collect them.
3. The States do not levy them.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only two statements are correct: 1 and 3. Taxes on transactions in stock exchanges and futures markets sit in the Union List, so Parliament makes the law, the Union levies them and the States do not. Statement 2 fails on collection: the Union also collects them. The split tempts because some Union-levied duties are collected by the States, which is a different arrangement. Remember: stock and futures taxes are levied and collected by the Union.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about indirect transfer in taxation:
1. It is the sale of shares of a foreign company whose value comes substantially from assets in India.
2. It covers an Indian company paying tax abroad on its foreign investment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. An indirect transfer is the sale of shares of a foreign company whose value comes substantially from assets in India: the shares are abroad but the value sits in India, so India claims a right to tax. Statement 2 widens the term to cover an Indian firm paying tax abroad, which is an ordinary cross-border investment. The word indirect tempts a loose reading. Remember: foreign shares, Indian value.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about capital gains:
1. A rise in the sales of a product is a capital gain.
2. A capital gain is taxed in the year in which the asset was acquired.
3. A painting is not a capital asset, so profit on its sale is not a capital gain.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. A capital gain is the profit on the transfer of a capital asset such as land, a building, shares or a painting. Statement 1 mistakes a business matter for it, since a rise in sales is not a capital gain. Statement 2 names the year of acquisition, whereas the gain is taxed in the year of transfer. Statement 3 excludes the painting, which is a capital asset. Each tempts by sounding like a plain rule. Remember: asset transferred, gain taxed that year.

qs.q:
In a simple model, money supply is M = m x H, where the money multiplier is m = (1 + c)/(c + r). Here H is high- powered money, c is the ratio of currency held by the public to deposits, and r is the reserve ratio. Take c =
0.25 and H = 1,200. The reserve ratio falls from 15 per cent to 12.5 per cent and H does not change. By how much can the money supply rise at most, once the system has fully adjusted?
qs.e: The rise is 250. At r = 15 per cent the multiplier is 1.25/0.4 = 3.125, so M = 3,750; at r = 12.5 per cent it is 1.25/0.375 = 3.33, so M = 4,000. The difference, 250, is an upper limit after full adjustment, not an instant result. The figure 4,000 is the new level and 3,750 the old one, while 1,600 comes from the simple 1/r rule, which leaves out the currency the public holds. Remember: the change is the new level minus the old level, and c belongs in the multiplier.

qs.q:
The figure given below shows two production possibilities curves for an economy that makes bikes and phones. Points A and B lie on the inner curve and point C lies on the outer curve. Consider the following observations: I. Point B has more bikes and fewer phones than point A, and both lie on the inner curve. II. Point C has more bikes and more phones than point B. III. The outer curve lies wholly outside the inner curve. Which of the following inferences can be drawn from the above statements?
1. The move from point A to point B shows growth in the economy's capacity to produce.
2. Reaching point C needs more resources or better technology, because shifting resources between the two goods cannot get there.
3. The move from point A to point B is a shift of resources between the two goods along one curve.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Inferences 2 and 3 can be drawn. A move between two points on one curve only changes the mix of bikes and phones, so it is a movement along the curve. Point C lies on the outer curve, which shows more of both goods, and that needs more resources or better technology. Inference 1 fails because growth appears as an outward shift of the whole curve, not as a move along it. It tempts because B has more bikes than A. Remember: outward shift is growth, movement along is reallocation.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. In 2015 the Government set up a new think tank by a resolution and it took over from the Planning Commission. The old body had a centralised, top-down and rigid design, gave the states little say, and had been shaped for a controlled economy. The new body was meant to foster cooperative federalism, innovation and enterprise. Like its predecessor, it is neither constitutional nor statutory. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The old design had been better suited to a market-oriented economy than to a controlled one.
2. One reason for the change was to give the states a stronger voice in planning.
3. The new body was created by an Act of Parliament.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 2.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The old body gave the states little say and the new one was meant to foster cooperative federalism, so a stronger voice for the states was one reason for the change. Statement 1 reverses the link, since the old design suited a controlled economy better than a market-oriented one. Statement 3 names the wrong source: the body was created by a Government resolution and is neither constitutional nor statutory. Statement 3 tempts because important bodies are often set up by statute. Remember: a resolution, not an Act, created the new think tank.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. By 1991 India held foreign exchange reserves worth a few weeks of imports. Over the years the Government's budget deficit had stayed high, borrowing from abroad had grown, prices had risen fast, public sector firms had done poorly and the country relied heavily on imports. Then the Gulf War of 1990-91 raised the price of oil and cut the money that Indians in the Gulf sent home. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The Gulf War cut the supply of foreign exchange from two sides, a dearer oil bill and smaller remittances.
2. The crisis had domestic causes that had built up before the Gulf War.
3. The Gulf War deepened an existing weakness and did not create it.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: All three statements are correct. A higher oil price raised the import bill while remittances from the Gulf fell, so foreign exchange was squeezed from both sides. The deficit, the foreign debt, the inflation, the weak public sector and the reliance on imports had all built up earlier, so the war drained reserves faster and was not the source of the weakness. A doubt arises because the war is the best-known event of the period. Remember: the Gulf War was the last push, not the first cause.

qs.q: The figure given below shows the path by which a rate decision reaches the real economy, with four links marked A, B, C and D, and the arrows give the order of the chain. The Reserve Bank cuts the policy repo rate. Which one of the following correctly places the change in what firms and families pay for credit, together with the channel through which it works?
o: At the link marked A, through the credit channel
At the link marked C, through the interest rate channel
At the link marked B, through the exchange rate channel, as the rupee reacts abroad
At the link marked D, through the interest rate channel
qs.e: The last option is correct. Monetary transmission is the path from a rate decision to what firms and families pay for credit, and the first place that cost changes is the rates banks charge on loans, the link marked D, through the interest rate channel. The link marked A is the decision itself, and C and B are what follow once credit costs change. The credit and exchange rate channels are other textbook routes and do not describe this link. Remember: the decision moves the lending rate first; spending and prices follow.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about human capital formation:
1. It raises the knowledge, skills and capacities of people mainly through spending on machines and buildings.
2. Spending on schooling and health adds to the stock of tangible assets such as machines and buildings.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Neither statement is correct. Human capital formation raises the knowledge, skills and capacities of people through education, health and training, so statement 1 fails on the means: machines and buildings are physical capital. Statement 2 swaps the kind of wealth, since schooling and health build intangible wealth in the form of skills and know-how. Both tempt because the two kinds of capital grow together, as machines raise output only when workers can use them. Remember: human capital is skill in people; physical capital is equipment.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about qualitative tools of credit control:
1. A margin requirement is the share of the value of a loan's security that the borrower must fund on his own.
2. A higher margin requirement means a smaller loan against the same security.
3. Moral suasion is persuasion by the central bank, with no force of law behind the request.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: All three statements are correct. A margin requirement is the part of the security's value that the borrower funds, a higher margin leaves a smaller loan against the same security, and moral suasion is persuasion by the central bank with no force of law behind it. A doubt arises on the third because the request comes from the central bank and so sounds like an order. Remember: a margin is the borrower's own share; moral suasion asks and does not compel.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about technical progress:
1. Training that makes each worker more productive is labour-augmenting technical progress.
2. A rise in the number of workers is labour-augmenting technical progress.
3. Replacing a wooden plough with a steel plough is capital-augmenting progress, because the improvement lies in the equipment.
4. Progress that raises output from given inputs without changing the best mix of capital and labour is neutral progress.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Training makes each worker better, the steel plough improves the equipment, and neutral progress raises output without changing the best mix of capital and labour. Statement 2 fails because more workers is a change in the size of the labour force and not a change in method or tool, so it is not technical progress. It tempts because the word labour appears in both. Remember: ask what the change improves, the worker or the equipment.

qs.q: Which one of the following best describes a mixed economy?
o: The state or the community owns production, and a central planning authority decides, so the price mechanism is weak.
Private and public ownership both exist; markets work, but the state regulates them and also produces in key sectors.
Private owners hold most of production, and markets and the profit motive decide, so the price mechanism dominates.
The state owns production and a planning authority fixes quantities, but markets are free to set every price.
qs.e: The second option is correct: a mixed economy has both private and public ownership, markets work, and the state regulates and also produces in key sectors. The first option describes a socialist or command economy, and the third a capitalist one. The fourth mixes a command feature with free prices and fits none of the three systems. The command case tempts because India's state owns firms. Remember: capitalist is private and market-led, command is state and planner-led, mixed has both.

qs.q:
Suppose a firm makes the following kinds of spending. Consider the following statements about how gross capital formation counts them:
1. Spending on software that the firm will use for years is counted as tangible capital.
2. Unsold goods added to the firm's inventories are counted as intangible capital.
3. Spending that builds brand value is counted as tangible capital, because it raises later sales.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. Software and brand value have no physical form yet give returns for years, so both are intangible, which breaks statements 1 and 3. Inventory, goods waiting to be sold, is the tangible item in such a list, which breaks statement 2. Statement 3 tempts because the extra sales it brings can be measured in money. Remember: software, research and brand are intangible; machines, roads and inventories are tangible.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Twelfth Plan and the figures used to describe the economy:
1. The Twelfth Plan covered the years 2012 to 2017.
2. The Twelfth Plan aimed at faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth.
3. A sector's share of GDP in an older series and its share of GVA in the new series rest on different bases and groupings, so the series must be named when a share is quoted.
4. The 8 per cent growth target of the Twelfth Plan was approved by Parliament on 27 December 2012.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Twelfth Plan covered 2012 to 2017 and aimed at faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth, and shares from the older GDP series and the newer GVA series come from different bases and groupings, so the series must be named. Statement 4 names the wrong body: the National Development Council approved the 8 per cent target on 27 December 2012. It tempts because Parliament seems the natural approver. Remember: the NDC approved the target; name the series when quoting a share.

qs.q:
Five people in a village have the following incomes, in thousands of rupees a year. A report quotes the mean as the income of a typical household. By what per cent does the mean income exceed the income of the middle person, the median?
1. Incomes of the first four people: 10, 10, 10 and 10.
2. Income of the fifth person: 60.
qs.e: The excess is 100 per cent. The mean is (10 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 60)/5 = 20 and the median is 10, so the excess is (20 - 10)/10 x 100 = 100 per cent. The figure 50 takes the median as a share of the mean, and 200 gives the mean as a share of the median, which is not the excess. The figure 600 compares the richest income with the median. Remember: one large income pulls the mean up, so the average hides what the middle person earns.

qs.q: Which one of the following correctly describes the Standing Deposit Facility of the Reserve Bank of India?
o: It lets banks borrow overnight at a rate 25 basis points above the repo rate by dipping into their SLR securities.
It is the facility under which the RBI lends to banks against approved securities at the policy repo rate.
It takes overnight deposits from banks against eligible government securities, and it forms the ceiling of the corridor.
It takes overnight deposits from banks without collateral and has been the floor of the corridor since April 2022.
qs.e: The last option is correct: the Standing Deposit Facility takes uncollateralised overnight deposits from LAF participants and, since April 2022, is the floor of the corridor, 25 basis points below the repo rate. The first option describes the Marginal Standing Facility, and the second describes repo. The third mixes in the collateral of reverse repo and wrongly calls the facility the ceiling. The first option tempts because the 25 basis points figure appears on both sides of the repo rate. Remember: SDF is the floor, 25 basis points below repo; MSF is the ceiling, 25 above.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about Gross Domestic Product:
1. A foreign firm producing goods in India adds to India's GDP.
2. An Indian firm producing goods in another country adds to India's GDP.
3. The value of technology work done in India by a global capability centre of a multinational counts in India's GDP, whoever owns the parent.
4. A rise in GDP raises health and schooling for the poor whatever happens to jobs, the sharing of income and state spending.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. GDP counts where production happens and not who owns the producer, so a foreign firm in India and a global capability centre doing work in India both add to it. Statement 2 reverses this, since an Indian firm producing abroad adds nothing. Statement 4 overreaches: growth reaches health and schooling only when there are jobs, income is widely shared and the state spends. It tempts because higher GDP does raise public revenue. Remember: GDP follows the territory, and growth does not secure development by itself.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. In one year the money supply rose after the Government drew funds from the Reserve Bank of India. In another year the money supply fell after the Reserve Bank sold government securities. On the basis of this passage and the working of base money, consider the following conclusions:
1. When the Government borrows from the RBI, the RBI pays by creating its own liability, which is new base money.
2. Government borrowing from the RBI and a sale of securities by the RBI move the money supply in the same direction.
3. Government borrowing from the RBI moves the money supply in the same direction as a purchase of securities by the RBI.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 3.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The RBI pays for the Government's borrowing with its own liability, new base money, which banks then multiply, so the money supply rises just as it does when the RBI buys securities. Statement 2 fails on direction: a sale of securities takes base money back and lowers the money supply. It tempts because both acts involve government paper. Remember: the RBI buying paper or lending to the Government creates base money; the RBI selling paper withdraws it.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about high-powered money:
1. It is also called reserve money, the monetary base and M0.
2. It is the sum of currency in circulation, bankers' deposits with the RBI and "other" deposits with the RBI.
3. Balances of the Government with the RBI form a part of it.
4. In 2025 the cut in the CRR and the open market purchases changed the quantity of money, while the cut in the repo rate changed its price.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Three statements are correct. High-powered money, also called reserve money, the monetary base and M0, is currency in circulation plus bankers' deposits plus "other" deposits with the RBI. The 2025 episode used the repo cut for the price of money and the CRR cut and open market purchases for its quantity. Statement 3 fails because Government balances with the RBI are not a component. It tempts because the Government banks with the RBI. Remember: bankers' and "other" deposits count; Government balances do not.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: India's import-substitution strategy began with the Second Plan, which built capital goods first.
Statement II: Capital goods are used to make other goods, so producing them at home first was meant to end the need for imports in the long run.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. The Second Plan followed the Mahalanobis strategy, building capital goods and heavy industry under public ownership in a determined thrust at replacing imports. Because capital goods make other goods, producing them first was meant to free the country from imports for good, which is why the Second Plan began import substitution with them. The Third Plan tempts because it fell short and faced a foreign exchange crisis. Remember: capital goods first, so import substitution starts with the Second Plan.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Customs duty : A product tax
2. Stamp and registration fees : A product tax
3. Fertiliser subsidy : A production subsidy
4. First Plan : Agriculture, irrigation and power first, because a weak farm base would have held back the rest of the economy
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Only two pairs are correctly matched. Customs duty is charged per unit of product, and the First Plan put agriculture, irrigation and power first because a weak farm base would have choked the rest of the economy. Stamp and registration fees are paid whatever the output, so they are a production tax. Fertiliser subsidy is paid per unit of product, so it is a product subsidy. Both swaps tempt because each item is a familiar tax or subsidy. Remember: per unit means product; whatever the output means production.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about growth and the capital-output link:
1. If the ICOR is treated as fixed, an investment rate of 32 per cent of GDP with an ICOR of 4 gives growth of about 8 per cent.
2. With the same investment rate and an ICOR of 6, growth is about 5.3 per cent.
3. Output of small unregistered businesses is estimated from surveys of unincorporated enterprises and the labour force, so a growth figure can be revised when new survey rounds arrive.
4. Since the 2015 revision India's headline growth is measured by GDP at constant market prices, while sector estimates are GVA at basic prices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: All four statements are correct. Growth is roughly the investment rate divided by the ICOR, so 32/4 gives 8 per cent and 32/6 gives about 5.3 per cent. Informal output is estimated from surveys and revised when new rounds arrive. Headline growth is GDP at constant market prices, while sector estimates are GVA at basic prices, which used to be at factor cost. A doubt arises because the ICOR rule is a simplification and the base is revised. Remember: growth is investment rate divided by ICOR; headline is GDP, sectors are GVA.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the aims of Indian planning:
1. The aims of Indian planning were growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity.
2. Modernisation means a rise in the capacity to produce goods and services, measured by GDP.
3. Growth alone gives equity, so the plans needed no separate aim for it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Indian planning had four aims: growth, modernisation, self-reliance and equity. Statement 2 gives the meaning of growth, which is measured by GDP, whereas modernisation is the adoption of new technology and new social attitudes. Statement 3 fails because growth alone does not give equity, since the gains may stay with a few, and that is why equity was carried as a separate aim. Statement 2 tempts because the two words sound alike. Remember: growth is measured by GDP, modernisation is new technology and attitudes, and equity needs its own aim.

qs.q: In a market for a crop, the quantity demanded is Qd = 100 - 2P and the quantity supplied is Qs = 2P + 20, where P is the price in rupees per unit. The Government fixes a legal minimum price of Rs 25 and buys the whole surplus at that price. How much money must it spend?
qs.e: The spending is Rs 500. At the floor of Rs 25, buyers want 100 - 50 = 50 units and sellers offer 50 + 20 = 70, so the surplus is 20 units, and 20 x 25 = Rs 500. The figure Rs 400 prices the surplus at the equilibrium price of Rs 20, and Rs 100 counts only the part above that price. The figure Rs 1,750 pays for all 70 units supplied, not just the surplus. Remember: a floor above equilibrium leaves a surplus, and the Government pays the floor price for each unit it buys.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Emergency was declared during the Fifth Plan.
2. The Fifth Plan was cut short in 1978, when the new government changed course.
3. The Fifth Plan aimed at removing poverty under the slogan Garibi Hatao and at self-reliance.
4. The Urjit Patel Committee of 2013-14 proposed a framework based on consumer prices, and the 2016 RBI Act amendment gave the inflation target and the MPC a legal base.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: All four statements are correct. The Fifth Plan, the plan of Garibi Hatao and self-reliance, saw the Emergency declared and elections bring the Janata Party to power, and it was cut short in 1978. The Urjit Patel Committee proposed a consumer-price framework, and the 2016 RBI Act amendment gave the target and the MPC a legal base. A doubt arises because 1980 and wholesale prices look like plausible slips. Remember: Fifth Plan cut short in 1978; inflation targeting rests on consumer prices.

qs.q: Which one of the following is true of the Eighth Plan?
o: It aimed at removing poverty under the slogan Garibi Hatao.
It followed the Mahalanobis strategy of building capital goods under public ownership.
It stressed growth with social justice and equity, with priority to agriculture and rural development.
It was the first plan of the reform era and moved planning from directive to indicative.
qs.e: The last option is correct: the Eighth Plan was the first plan of the reform era and moved planning from directive to indicative. The first option belongs to the Fifth Plan, the second to the Second Plan, and the third to the Ninth Plan. The Ninth Plan tempts because it also came after the reforms. Remember: Eighth Plan means first reform-era plan; Ninth Plan means social justice and rural priority.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the rupee and the Reserve Bank: I. If interest rates abroad fall, capital tends to flow into India. II. Capital flowing into India pushes the rupee up. III. If the rupee falls fast, the RBI sells dollars. Which of the following relationships among the above statements is/are correct?
1. Statement I explains why the RBI sells dollars as described in Statement III.
2. Statement I helps to explain Statement II.
3. Statements II and III describe opposite pressures on the rupee, and the RBI buys dollars in the first case and sells them in the second.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Relationships 2 and 3 are correct. A fall in rates abroad sends capital into India, which is why the rupee is pushed up, and the RBI buying dollars is the usual response; when the rupee falls fast the pressure is the opposite and the RBI sells dollars. Relationship 1 fails because the fall in foreign rates produces the first case, not the second. It tempts because both situations involve the RBI trading dollars. Remember: rupee rising, RBI buys dollars; rupee falling fast, RBI sells dollars.

qs.q:
The figure given below plots the income index of the Human Development Index against gross national income per capita on a linear axis. Points A and B show incomes of 2,000 and 4,000 dollars, and points C and D show 30,000 and 60,000 dollars. Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The rise in the income index from point A to point B is the same as the rise from point C to point D, although the second needs fifteen times as many extra dollars.
Statement II: The income index uses the natural log of income, so each doubling of income adds the same amount.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. Each move is a doubling, 2,000 to 4,000 and 30,000 to 60,000 dollars, and with a log each doubling adds the same amount to the index, about 0.10 in both cases. The extra dollars are 2,000 against 30,000, fifteen times as many. This reflects diminishing returns, since an extra dollar matters more to a poor person. The second option tempts because the curve looks like two unrelated slopes. Remember: log income means equal doublings add equal index gains.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bank Rate:
1. The Bank Rate is the rate at which banks park their surplus cash with the RBI.
2. The Bank Rate is the penal rate for shortfalls in the CRR and the SLR, and it is aligned with the MSF rate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The Bank Rate is the rate at which the RBI buys or rediscounts eligible bills of exchange, it is the penal rate on shortfalls in the CRR and SLR, and it is published under Section 49 of the RBI Act and is aligned with the MSF rate. Statement 1 fails because parking surplus cash with the RBI is done at the SDF rate, the floor of the corridor. It tempts because both are RBI rates in the same corridor. Remember: Bank Rate is for bills and penalties, the SDF is for parking cash.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A government that builds a flyover gives up the school that the same money could have built, and that school is the opportunity cost of the flyover.
2. A cut in the CRR lowers the reserve ratio, so it raises the money multiplier and also frees funds for lending.
3. When the Government supplies a good free, the opportunity cost disappears, because the users pay nothing for it.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only two statements are correct. The school given up is the value of the next best use of the money, which is the opportunity cost of the flyover, and a CRR cut lowers r, so the multiplier rises and funds are freed for lending. Statement 3 fails on the word disappears: inputs were still used and someone paid for them, so the cost moves from the users to the tax-paying public. It tempts because the user's own bill is zero. Remember: free to the user is never free to the economy.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a Human Development Index group and its range of values at present:
1. Very high human development : 0.750 and above
2. High human development : 0.650 to 0.799
3. Medium human development : 0.550 to 0.699
4. Low human development : below 0.500
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Only one pair is correctly matched. Medium is 0.550 to 0.699, and the cut-offs of 0.800, 0.700 and 0.550 have stood unchanged since the 2014 report. The first pair fails on 0.750, because very high starts at 0.800. The second fails on 0.650, because high starts at 0.700. The fourth fails on 0.500, because low is below 0.550. The wrong figures tempt because older tables quote lower bands. Remember: three cut-offs, 0.800, 0.700 and 0.550.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about services in India, on the figures reported in 2026, is correct?
o: Services provide more than half of gross value added, yet they employ about 30 per cent of the workforce on a NITI Aayog estimate.
Services provide about 30 per cent of gross value added, yet they employ more than half of the workforce on a NITI Aayog estimate.
Services gave 61.9 per cent of employment in the whole workforce in the first half of 2025-26 and about 30 per cent of urban employment.
Services provide less than half of gross value added, yet they employ about 30 per cent of the workforce on a NITI Aayog estimate.
qs.e: Services give more than half of gross value added but employ about 30 per cent of the workforce on the NITI Aayog estimate, so the job share is well below the output share. The second option reverses the two shares. The third swaps the figures: 61.9 per cent is the share of urban employment in the first half of 2025-26. The fourth puts the output share below half. The urban figure tempts because it is the most precise number. Remember: about 30 per cent of all jobs, 61.9 per cent of urban jobs.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the crisis of 1991 and the reforms that followed:
1. India's foreign exchange reserves had fallen to a few months of imports by 1991, which brought on a balance of payments crisis.
2. The rupee was devalued in a single step in July 1991, under Prime Minister Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Manmohan Singh.
3. Devaluation and deficit control are structural adjustment, while delicensing and trade opening are stabilisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. Reserves had fallen to a few weeks of imports, not months. The rupee was devalued in two steps in the first days of July 1991, not in one. Stabilisation means quick, short-term fixes, such as devaluation and deficit control, while structural adjustment means longer-term reforms, such as delicensing and trade opening, so statement 3 reverses them. Each statement keeps real names and events, which is why each tempts. Remember: weeks of imports, two steps of devaluation, stabilisation is the quick fix.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the costs of a firm in the short run:
1. Variable costs do not change with output, while fixed costs rise with it.
2. Average cost is total cost divided by output, and average fixed cost always falls as output rises, because the same fixed sum is spread over more units.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Average cost is total cost divided by output, and the fixed sum is spread over more units as output grows, so average fixed cost falls, as in the table that runs 60, 30, 20, 15, 12 and 10. Statement 1 swaps the two kinds of cost: fixed costs stay put in the short run and variable costs rise with output, and total cost is their sum. It tempts because both words describe costs that appear on the same schedule. Remember: fixed stays put, variable moves with output.

qs.q: A bank has net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) of Rs 2,500 crore. The CRR is 4 per cent and the SLR is 20 per cent of NDTL. Assume that, apart from these two requirements, the bank has no other claim on its funds. How much is left for lending?
qs.e: The amount left is 2,500 x (1 - 0.04 - 0.20) = 1,900 crore. The CRR keeps 100 crore with the RBI and the SLR needs 500 crore in securities, cash and gold, so 600 crore is tied up and 1,900 crore remains. Rs 2,400 crore takes off only the CRR and Rs 2,000 crore only the SLR, while Rs 600 crore is the amount tied up, not the amount left. Remember: take both ratios off NDTL, then see what is left.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. A clerk is paid Rs 50,000 a month, and on the day the pay arrives her bank account shows a balance of Rs 1,20,000. A factory owns machines worth Rs 8 crore and, in the year, makes goods worth Rs 3 crore. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The monthly pay is a flow and the bank balance is a stock.
2. The value of the factory's machines is a flow, because it is measured over a year.
3. GDP and wealth are both stocks, because each is a sum of value.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only conclusion 1 is correct. Pay of Rs 50,000 a month is a flow, measured over a stretch of time, and the bank balance is a stock, measured at one moment. Conclusion 2 fails because machines are a stock; the goods made in the year are the flow. Conclusion 3 fails because GDP is a flow measured over a year, while wealth is a stock. Both tempt because a rupee value is attached to each item. Remember: flow over a period, stock at a moment.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. A customer offers a shopkeeper a cheque for Rs 5,000 for goods, and the shopkeeper declines it but accepts the same sum in notes. The customer then offers to settle another bill of Rs 1,500 wholly in one-rupee coins in a single payment. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The shopkeeper may refuse the cheque, because a cheque is bank money accepted by agreement and the law does not compel anyone to take it.
2. The shopkeeper must accept the whole Rs 1,500 in one-rupee coins, because coins are legal tender for any amount.
3. Bank deposits become legal tender once they are widely used for payment.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only conclusion 1 is correct. Cheques, drafts and bank deposits are bank money accepted by agreement, and the law does not force anyone to take them. Conclusion 2 fails because coins of Rs 1 and above are legal tender only up to Rs 1,000 in one payment, so Rs 1,500 in one payment may be refused. Conclusion 3 fails because wide use does not create legal tender; the law must compel the creditor. Coins tempt because notes have no limit. Remember: legal tender compels the creditor, and agreement does not.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Governor draws authority from the RBI Act, and the Centre's power to give directions to the RBI comes from Section 7 of the same Act.
2. The Centre's power to direct the RBI comes from a provision of the Constitution and not from the RBI Act.
3. Since 1980 the share of the tertiary sector in India's GDP has shown a falling trend.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only one statement is correct. The Governor draws authority from the RBI Act, and the Centre's power to direct the RBI also comes from that Act, in Section 7, and not from the Constitution. Statement 2 gives the power a constitutional source, which it does not have. Statement 3 reverses the trend: the tertiary share of GDP has been rising since 1980. The Constitution tempts because the Governor and the Centre seem to hold constitutional powers. Remember: Section 7 of the RBI Act, not the Constitution.

qs.q: The figure given below shows India's real GDP growth for seven years on the 2011-12 base, with the figure for 2024-25 a provisional estimate as reported in 2025. Which one of the following claims about the years shown is correct?
o: Growth fell below zero in 2020-21 and was highest in the next year.
Growth rose steadily over the years shown from the first to the last.
Growth in 2023-24 was higher than growth in the recovery year 2021-22.
Growth after the fall of 2020-21 was lower in each later year than before.
qs.e: The first claim is correct: growth was minus 5.8 per cent in 2020-21 and 9.7 per cent in 2021-22, the highest of the seven years. A claim of steady increase fails because the series swings from 8.3 to 3.9, to minus 5.8 and back to 9.7. The 2023-24 figure of 9.2 is below 9.7, not above it. After the fall, growth went 9.7, 7.6, 9.2 and 6.5, which is not a steady decline. Mistakes tempt because the later years look high. Remember: swings, not steady growth, mark the series.

qs.q:
Consider the following observations about a government hospital that treats patients without a charge: I. The hospital uses doctors' time, medicines and buildings that have to be paid for. II. The payments for those inputs come from the taxes that the public pays. III. Patients pay nothing at the counter for their treatment. Which of the following inferences can be drawn from the above statements?
1. The cost of the treatment has moved from the patients to the tax-paying public.
2. Because patients pay nothing, the opportunity cost of the treatment has fallen to zero.
3. The doctors' time, medicines and buildings could have been put to another use, so an opportunity cost remains.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Inferences 1 and 3 can be drawn. The inputs were used and paid for out of taxes, so the cost has moved from the users to the tax-paying public, and since the same inputs had other uses an opportunity cost remains. Inference 2 fails because a zero bill at the counter does not make the cost zero; the cost has only moved to another payer. It tempts because the patient sees no charge and so seems to bear no cost. Remember: free to the user is never free to the economy.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about narrow money, M1:
1. M1 adds together the currency held by the public, the demand deposits in the banking system and the "other" deposits held with the RBI.
2. Cash that banks hold in their own vaults is counted in the currency part of M1.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. M1 is currency with the public plus demand deposits with the banking system plus the other deposits with the RBI. Statement 2 fails because the currency in M1 is the currency with the public, and bank vault cash is excluded; counting it would count the same rupee twice. It tempts because vault cash is also currency. Remember: M1 counts cash in public hands, not cash in bank vaults.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of an activity and the sector of the economy to which it belongs:
1. Mineral exploration : Tertiary sector
2. Electricity, gas and water supply : Secondary sector
3. Storage of agricultural produce : Primary sector
4. Weaving cloth : Tertiary sector
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Only one pair is correctly matched. Electricity, gas and water supply sits in the secondary sector with manufacturing and construction. Exploration is part of mining and so primary, though it sounds like a service. Storage of produce is a service, so it is tertiary and not primary because it handles farm goods. Weaving turns yarn into cloth, so it is secondary and not tertiary. The common error is to read the sound of the word rather than the activity. Remember: exploration is primary, storage is tertiary.

qs.q:
The figure given below shows four demand curves marked A, B, C and D, drawn on the same axes. Consider the following statements:
1. Over the range shown, the curve marked A is flat enough for demand along it to be elastic, with elasticity above 1.
2. The curve marked C is vertical, so demand along it is perfectly inelastic, with an elasticity of 0.
3. The curve marked D is horizontal, so demand along it is perfectly inelastic.
4. Over the range shown, a rise in price along the curve marked B would raise the seller's total revenue, because demand on this steep curve is inelastic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The flat curve A is elastic, the vertical curve C is perfectly inelastic at 0, and the steep curve B is inelastic, so the quantity falls by a smaller share than the price rises and revenue goes up. Statement 3 fails because the horizontal curve D is perfectly elastic, with elasticity at infinity. It tempts because horizontal and vertical are easily swapped. Remember: vertical means zero response, horizontal means infinite response.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about an economy over a long period: I. National income rises several times over. II. Population grows almost as fast as national income. III. Per capita income barely changes. Which of the following relationships among the above statements is/are correct?
1. Statement II explains why Statement III holds despite Statement I, because population is the denominator of per capita income.
2. Poverty among the people, and not Statement II, is what explains Statement III.
3. Statements I and III can hold together because Statement II raises the denominator by almost as much as the numerator has risen.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Relationships 1 and 3 are correct. Per capita income is national income divided by population, so a denominator that grows nearly as fast as the numerator cancels the gain and the average barely moves. Relationship 2 fails because poverty is a separate fact; it does not explain why the average fails to rise. It tempts because a low average sounds like a sign of poor people. Remember: the average moves with the numerator and the denominator, and poverty is not the cause.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A farmer's plough is fixed capital because it serves for many seasons, while the yarn that a weaver uses is working capital.
2. Cash kept to meet day-to-day payments is fixed capital, since a firm holds it all year.
3. Per capita income is national income divided by population, and it shows the average income per head.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. A plough is used for many seasons, so it is fixed capital, while yarn is consumed by the cloth, so it is working capital. Per capita income is national income divided by population and shows the average income per head. Statement 2 fails because cash for day-to-day running is working capital; fixed capital is equipment and buildings used again and again. It tempts because a firm keeps some cash all year. Remember: fixed capital is used again and again, working capital is used up or runs the day.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a kind of good and what marks it:
1. Merit goods : Positive externalities, so markets supply too little of them
2. Demerit goods : Positive externalities, so markets supply too little of them
3. Public goods : Both excludable and rivalrous
4. Private goods : Both non-rival and non-excludable
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Only one pair is correctly matched. Merit goods carry positive externalities and are under-supplied by markets. Demerit goods carry negative externalities and are over-consumed, so the second pair fails. Public goods are non-rival and non-excludable, and private goods are both excludable and rivalrous, so the third and fourth pairs swap the two kinds. The swaps tempt because the two lists of terms look alike. Remember: merit means positive and under-supplied, demerit means negative and over-consumed.

qs.q:
A farmer grows wheat and sells it to a miller, the miller sells flour to a baker and the baker sells bread to a family. Consider the following statements:
1. The wheat and the flour are intermediate goods, and the bread is the final good.
2. Adding the sales of wheat, flour and bread counts the wheat only once, because it is used up in the flour.
3. If just two firms supplied all the flour, the market would be a duopoly, the smallest oligopoly, and the flour would still be an intermediate good.
4. If a higher price of bread raises the quantity of bread supplied, the extra bread is counted once in final output and the flour used for it is not counted again.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Wheat and flour are used up in making something else, while bread receives no further value added. Two firms make a duopoly, yet the flour stays intermediate; a higher price raises the quantity of bread supplied, and counting only final output keeps the flour from being counted again. Statement 2 fails because adding every sale counts the wheat in the flour and again in the bread, which is double counting. It tempts because the wheat is used up once. Remember: count final goods only, or the value added at each stage.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about what would follow in each case:
1. If heavy capital inflows lead the RBI to buy dollars, the rupees it pays out add to liquidity, and an issue of securities under the Market Stabilisation Scheme, begun in 2004, would absorb that liquidity.
2. If the RBI absorbs surplus liquidity from large capital inflows under the Market Stabilisation Scheme, it does so by issuing short-dated government securities and treasury bills.
3. If the RBI uses the Market Stabilisation Scheme to absorb surplus liquidity, the cash raised is added to the RBI's own income and not held in a separate government account.
4. If the RBI buys US$10 billion at an assumed Rs 85 a dollar and then sells securities worth the rupees it paid out, the net change in liquidity is zero.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Three statements are correct. A dollar purchase pays out rupees and adds liquidity, and an MSS issue, begun in 2004, takes it back; the MSS absorbs large inflows by issuing short-dated securities and treasury bills; and a sale worth the Rs 850 billion paid out leaves the net change at zero. Statement 3 fails because the cash is held in a separate government account with the RBI and not in the RBI's own income. It tempts because the RBI runs the sale. Remember: the MSS cash sits in a separate government account.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the limits of GDP:
Statement I: Damage that a user does to a river is left out of GDP, because the loss falls on others outside the sale and no deduction is made for it.
Statement II: Unpaid household and care work is left out of GDP, because no price is recorded for it.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct, and Statement II does not explain Statement I. Each gap in GDP has its own cause: river damage is left out because the loss falls on others outside the sale and no deduction is made for it, and unpaid work is left out because no price is recorded for it. The first gap is a spill-over onto others and the second is a missing market price, so each has its own cause. Remember: each gap in GDP has its own cause, and one does not explain the other.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: Raising the MSF rate is a tightening step, which an expansionary RBI would not take.
Statement II: A higher MSF rate lowers the cost of emergency funds for banks, and so it encourages lending.
Statement III: A rise in the MSF rate leaves the Bank Rate unchanged, because the Bank Rate is set separately from the MSF rate.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct, and neither Statement II nor Statement III is. A higher MSF rate raises the cost of emergency funds and discourages lending, which is why raising it is a tightening step. Statement II reverses that effect. Statement III fails because the Bank Rate moves automatically with the MSF rate, so a rise in one carries the other up. Statement III tempts because the Bank Rate has its own role in rediscounting bills. Remember: MSF up, Bank Rate up, lending down.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Development Council:
1. It was set up in 1952.
2. It is a statutory body, set up by an Act of Parliament, and the Prime Minister presides over it.
3. It was the apex body linking the Centre and the states on plans, and Chief Ministers were among its members.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only two statements are correct. The NDC was set up in 1952, and it was the apex body linking the Centre and the states on plans, with Union Cabinet ministers, Chief Ministers and administrators of Union Territories as members. Statement 2 fails on the source: like the Planning Commission, the NDC is neither constitutional nor statutory, though the Prime Minister did preside. It tempts because the chair is correct. Remember: the NDC has no Act behind it, and the Prime Minister chaired it.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about services in India: I. Services produce more than half of gross value added. II. Services employ about 30 per cent of the workforce on a NITI Aayog estimate. III. A large part of the output of services comes from finance and information technology, which earn a lot of value per worker and employ few. Which of the following relationships among the above statements is/are correct?
1. Statement III helps to explain why the job share in Statement II is lower than the output share in Statement I.
2. Statements I and II together suggest that a service-led economy creates fewer jobs than its output share would suggest.
