Consider the following statements about e-RUPI and the digital rupee: I. e-RUPI is a prepaid, single-use digital voucher delivered by SMS or QR code and tied to a person and a purpose. II. The retail e-rupee is a digital token that represents legal tender and is held in bank-run wallets. III. e-RUPI is not the digital currency being considered by the RBI. Consider the following claims about how these statements are related:
1. The difference between the instruments in Statements I and II explains why Statement III holds, since a prepaid voucher is not a token of legal tender.
2. Statement I describes the retail e-rupee and Statement II describes e-RUPI.
3. Statement III shows that e-RUPI and the e-rupee are two names for the same instrument.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Only relationship 1 is correct. e-RUPI is a prepaid voucher, while the retail e-rupee is a token of legal tender, so e-RUPI is not the digital currency being considered by the RBI. Relationship 2 swaps the instruments, since the voucher delivered by SMS or QR code is e-RUPI. Relationship 3 reverses Statement III, which separates the two rather than joining them. It tempts because the names are alike. Remember: e-RUPI is a voucher; the e- rupee is a token of legal tender.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Measuring a qubit that is in superposition leaves it holding many configurations at once.
2. Training tunes a model's adjustable settings so that answers improve, while inference is using the trained model on new data.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. A model is an algorithm with adjustable parameters: training tunes them, and using the trained model on new data is inference. Statement 1 reverses the effect of measurement: superposition lets qubits represent many configurations at once, but measuring collapses the state to a single 0 or 1. It tempts because superposition is described as holding many states. Remember: superposition before measuring, one value after; training tunes, inference uses.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Below its transition temperature a superconductor loses all resistance and also expels a magnetic field, so a magnet can float above it.
A shape-memory alloy bent when cold stays bent when it is heated, and Nitinol, a nickel-titanium alloy, is the best-known example of one.
Conventional superconductors generally lose their electrical resistance only when cooled below about 200 K (minus 73 degrees Celsius).
The Meissner effect is a superconductor drawing in a magnetic field as it is cooled, so that a magnet placed near it sticks to it.
qs.e: The first statement is correct: below the transition temperature a superconductor shows zero resistance and also expels a magnetic field, the Meissner effect, which lets a magnet float above a cooled copper-oxide superconductor. The second fails because a shape-memory alloy bent when cold returns to its shape when heated. The third inflates the number: for conventional superconductors the transition is generally below 20 K. The fourth reverses the Meissner effect, which pushes the field out. Remember: zero resistance and field expelled; shape-memory alloys spring back when heated.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about materials, networks and computers:
1. Graphene conducts electricity about as well as copper, but it conducts heat less well than copper does.
2. Graphene is almost transparent, and helium passes through it easily.
3. Tor sends traffic through several volunteer relays and encrypts it at each step, so that every relay learns the whole path.
4. Supercomputers named PARAM Siddhi, Pravega and Ganga were built under the National Blockchain Framework.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. Graphene conducts electricity about as well as copper and heat better than any other known material, and it is almost transparent yet helium cannot pass through it. In Tor each relay learns only the next hop, not the whole path. The PARAM machines were built under the National Supercomputing Mission, not the National Blockchain Framework. Each statement tempts because it changes one word of a true fact. Remember: graphene beats copper at heat; Tor relays see one hop; PARAM belongs to the Supercomputing Mission.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023:
1. A Data Fiduciary is the person to whom the personal data relates.
2. A Data Fiduciary is the party that decides why and how personal data is processed.
3. For a child, the Data Principal includes the parent or guardian.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. A Data Fiduciary decides why and how personal data is processed, and a Data Principal is the person the data relates to; for a child, the Data Principal includes the parent or guardian. Statement 1 swaps the two terms and gives the Data Principal definition to the Data Fiduciary. It tempts because a fiduciary sounds like the owner of the data. Remember: the Fiduciary decides; the Principal is the person.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. Two blockchains choose who adds the next block. On network P, nodes compete to find a nonce that makes the block header's hash fall below a target; finding it is costly, but checking it takes one hash. On network Q, the chance of publishing a block depends on the share of cryptocurrency a user has staked, which avoids heavy computation. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. Network P uses proof of work, and checking a winning nonce is far cheaper than finding it.
2. Network Q uses much more energy than network P, because staking needs heavy computation.
3. On network P the chance of publishing a block depends on the share of cryptocurrency staked.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Proof of work makes nodes compete for a nonce, which is costly to find and cheap to check by one hash. Statement 2 reverses the energy comparison: proof of stake avoids heavy computation, so network Q uses less energy. Statement 3 swaps the two methods, since the share staked decides the chance on network Q, while on network P it is the first valid nonce. It tempts because both methods choose a block-maker. Remember: work means a nonce race and heavy energy; stake means share held and no heavy computation.

qs.q:
Arrange the following events in the order in which they happened:
1. The European Council grants Ukraine candidate status
2. Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine
3. IMEC is announced, with Italy among its founding signatories
4. Ukraine applies to join the European Union
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: The order is the invasion of February 2022, Ukraine's application on 28 February 2022, candidate status on 23 June 2022, and the announcement of IMEC in 2023, of which Italy is a founding signatory. Putting candidacy before the application reverses the process, and putting the application before the invasion mistakes the diplomatic reply for its cause. Placing IMEC before candidacy treats a 2023 corridor as an older event. Remember: war in February, application within days, candidacy in June, corridor a year later.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the Pacific region:
1. FIPIC, the Forum for India-Pacific Islands Cooperation, was launched on 19 November 2014 during Prime Minister Modi's visit to Fiji.
2. Kiribati, Nauru and Palau are among the Pacific islands grouped as Micronesia, while Fiji and Vanuatu belong to Melanesia.
3. India's trade with Australia leans towards textiles and pharmaceuticals, which is one source of friction between the two.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. FIPIC was launched on 19 November 2014 during Modi's visit to Fiji, and the Pacific islands fall into Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia, with Kiribati, Nauru and Palau in the second group. Statement 3 fails on the goods: friction with Australia arises because trade is skewed to minerals and energy. It tempts because textiles and pharmaceuticals are the usual Indian exports. Remember: Australian trade tilts to minerals and energy, not to textiles.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about disputes at sea in East Asia:
1. The unanimous award of 12 July 2016 in the Philippines' case against China also decided which state owns the features of the Spratly Islands.
2. The Senkaku Islands, which Japan administers and China also claims, are part of the South China Sea dispute, in which the tribunal placed Mischief Reef and Second Thomas Shoal within the Philippines' EEZ.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Neither statement is correct. The 2016 UNCLOS award, given unanimously, settled the legal status of features and maritime rights, not who owns any land feature, so statement 1 overreaches. Statement 2 pairs a true finding, the Philippines' EEZ around Mischief Reef and Second Thomas Shoal, with a false link: the Senkakus, administered by Japan and claimed by China, belong to the separate East China Sea dispute. Both are maritime disputes involving China, which tempts the join. Remember: the award fixed rights and status, not ownership; the Senkakus lie in the East China Sea.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the trade pacts of the ASEAN region:
1. India withdrew from the RCEP negotiations in November 2019 and is not a member of the pact.
2. The 2020 ministers' declaration lets India start accession talks with RCEP at any time after the pact enters into force.
3. AITIGA is the ASEAN-India Trade in Goods Agreement, and its rules of origin test whether a good was made in a partner country and so earns the lower tariff.
4. In the review of AITIGA, India wants to fix its deficit, tighten rules of origin and stop third-country goods being routed through ASEAN.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: All four statements are correct. India left the RCEP talks in November 2019 and stays outside, yet the 2020 declaration leaves the door to accession talks open after entry into force. AITIGA is the goods agreement, and rules of origin decide which goods earn the lower tariff; in the review India seeks a smaller deficit, firmer origin rules and an end to routing through ASEAN. Doubt may arise from the belief that leaving closed the door for good. Remember: India is outside RCEP, but the door stays open.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about NATO and its European members:
1. Article 5 treats an armed attack on one ally in Europe or North America as an attack on all, but each ally then takes the action it judges necessary and need not send troops.
2. Austria, Cyprus, Ireland and Sweden are the four members of the European Union that stand outside NATO.
3. Finland became the 32nd member of NATO on 7 March 2024, after Sweden had joined in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Article 5 makes an attack on one ally an attack on all, yet each ally chooses the action it thinks necessary, so troops are not compulsory. Statement 2 names Sweden among the EU states outside NATO, but Malta is the fourth, since Sweden joined. Statement 3 swaps the two accessions: Finland joined in 2023 and Sweden became the 32nd member on 7 March 2024. The swaps tempt because the two Nordic states moved together. Remember: Finland first in 2023, Sweden 32nd in March 2024; Malta stays out.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about the Korean peninsula and India's ties with South Korea is correct?
o: The peninsula was divided in 1945, and the war of 1950 to 1953 ended with a peace treaty between the two sides.
India's Special Strategic Partnership with South Korea, the highest tier, came in 2010, the year of the CEPA.
The peninsula was divided in 1945, the war ended with an armistice, and the Special Strategic Partnership of 2015 is the highest tier.
India wants markets beyond China and a larger Indo-Pacific role from Korea, while Korea seeks investment, technology and shipbuilding.
qs.e: The third statement is correct. The peninsula was divided in 1945, the war of 1950 to 1953 ended with an armistice and not a peace treaty, and the Special Strategic Partnership of 2015 is the highest tier of India-Korea ties. The first fails on the word treaty. The second moves the highest tier back to 2010, when the Strategic Partnership and the CEPA came. The fourth swaps the wants: India seeks investment, technology and shipbuilding, and Korea seeks markets beyond China. Remember: armistice, not peace treaty; highest tier in 2015, not 2010.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about ASEAN is correct?
o: It was founded in Bangkok on 8 August 1967 by five states, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand, and its Charter took effect in 2008.
It was founded on 8 August 1967 by five states that included Vietnam and Brunei, and its Secretariat is in Jakarta, the city of its Charter.
It follows the ASEAN way of majority voting and non-interference, and its motto is One Vision, One Identity, One Community, as in its Charter.
Its Secretariat is in Bangkok, where the ASEAN Declaration was signed, and its leaders hold a summit twice a year, with ministers meeting more often.
qs.e: The first statement is correct: ASEAN was founded in Bangkok on 8 August 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand, and the Charter has been in effect from 15 December 2008. The second names Vietnam and Brunei, which joined in 1995 and 1984. The third replaces consensus with majority voting. The fourth puts the Secretariat in Bangkok, but it is in Jakarta. Bangkok is only the place of signing, which tempts the fourth. Remember: signed in Bangkok, housed in Jakarta; consensus, not majority.

qs.q: In the figure given below, four of the eight member states of the Arctic Council are marked A, B, C and D. The council was formed by the Ottawa Declaration of 1996 and leaves out military security, and India takes part as an observer. Which one of the following correctly identifies the state that hosts India's Arctic research station Himadri, the state that runs the LeadIT initiative with India and the state that has a Green Strategic Partnership with India?
o: Himadri lies in the state marked B, LeadIT is run with the state marked A, and the Green Strategic Partnership is with the state marked C.
Himadri lies in the state marked A, LeadIT is run with the state marked C, and the Green Strategic Partnership is with the state marked B.
Himadri lies in the state marked A, LeadIT is run with the state marked B, and the Green Strategic Partnership is with the state marked C.
Himadri lies in the state marked D, LeadIT is run with the state marked B, and the Green Strategic Partnership is with the state marked C.
qs.e: The third option is correct. Himadri stands at Svalbard in Norway, marked A; Sweden, marked B, runs LeadIT with India; and Denmark, marked C, has the Green Strategic Partnership. The first swaps Norway and Sweden. The second swaps Sweden and Denmark. The fourth places Himadri in Finland, marked D, which is a council member but has no Svalbard station. The Nordic states look alike, which makes the swaps tempting. Remember: Himadri in Norway, LeadIT with Sweden, Green Strategic Partnership with Denmark.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and Japan:
1. Indian analysts blame standards, certification and project delays, not tariffs, for the thin trade between the two countries, and a 2+2 dialogue joins two foreign and two defence ministers.
2. Japan is a treaty ally of the United States and joined sanctions on Russia after 2022 while India did not, and Japan seeks capital and technology from India while India wants a manufacturing partner beyond China.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. Indian analysts name standards, certification and project delays, not tariffs, as the cause of thin trade, and a 2+2 dialogue joins two foreign and two defence ministers. Statement 2 starts with true frictions, the US alliance and Russia sanctions, but then reverses the wants: India seeks capital, technology and supply chains, and Japan seeks a manufacturing partner beyond China. The true opening makes the swap hard to spot. Remember: India asks for capital and technology; Japan asks for a partner beyond China.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of an Indo-Pacific version and its description:
1. India's Indo-Pacific vision : a free, open and inclusive order resting on ASEAN centrality, set out by Prime Minister Modi in Singapore on 1 June 2018
2. Japan's Free and Open Indo-Pacific : often traced to Prime Minister Abe's 2007 speech in India's Parliament
3. ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific : adopted in June 2019, creating new forums to replace the existing ASEAN-led ones
4. Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative : set out by Prime Minister Modi in Singapore on 1 June 2018 Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
qs.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. India's vision, resting on ASEAN centrality, was set out in Singapore on 1 June 2018, and Japan's FOIP is often traced to Abe's 2007 speech. Pair 3 reverses the Outlook, which strengthens existing ASEAN-led forums and creates none. Pair 4 gives the Singapore speech to the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, which was launched at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok on 4 November 2019. Both Indian versions tempt confusion. Remember: speech in Singapore for the vision, summit in Bangkok for IPOI.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and ASEAN:
1. The first ASEAN-India Summit was held in Phnom Penh in 2002, and India joined the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation on 8 October 2003.
2. The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership came in 2012 and the Strategic Partnership on 12 November
2022.
3. The Delhi Declaration of 25 January 2018 named the maritime domain a key area, and all ten ASEAN leaders were guests at the Republic Day parade that year.
4. The India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway runs from Moreh in Manipur to Mae Sot in Thailand, and its extension to Cambodia, Lao PDR and Vietnam is under consideration.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Three statements are correct. The summit at Phnom Penh in 2002, the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation on 8 October 2003, the Delhi Declaration of 25 January 2018 with all ten leaders at the parade, and the Moreh to Mae Sot highway with extension only under consideration all hold. Statement 2 swaps the tiers: the Strategic Partnership dates from 2012 and the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership from 12 November 2022. The words differ by one adjective, which tempts the swap. Remember: strategic in 2012, comprehensive strategic in 2022.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about Taiwan and India:
1. The People's Republic of China claims Taiwan as its territory, and the Nationalist government moved to Taiwan in 1945 at the end of the Chinese civil war.
2. India has formal diplomatic ties with Taiwan, and its two offices, in Taipei and New Delhi, were set up in
1995.
3. India's Cabinet approved an investment agreement between the two offices, and because China objects to official contact, India keeps contact political and strategic.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. The Nationalist government moved to Taiwan in 1949, not 1945, at the end of the Chinese civil war, although the claim by the People's Republic of China is stated correctly. India has no formal ties with Taiwan, and the offices of 1995 are not embassies. Because China objects to official contact, India keeps contact economic and cultural, not political and strategic. Each statement keeps a true frame and alters one element. Remember: 1949 move, offices of 1995, contact economic and cultural.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs about the South China Sea:
1. India's stated position : not a claimant but a user of the lanes, taking no side on who owns the features
2. Tribunal finding on Scarborough Shoal : a territorial sea but no EEZ
3. China and the award : China did not accept or take part, and the tribunal can enforce the award with its own police force
4. Tribunal finding on Itu Aba : a full EEZ, as the largest high-tide feature of the Spratlys
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Only two pairs are correctly matched. India's stated position is that it is a user of the lanes and takes no side on ownership, and Scarborough Shoal received a territorial sea but no EEZ. Pair 3 keeps China's non- acceptance but adds enforcement: the award is final and binding, yet the tribunal has no police or army. Pair 4 fails because Itu Aba and other high-tide features are rocks, with no EEZ. Remember: the award binds but cannot be enforced, and rocks earn no EEZ.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about European bodies:
1. The Council of Europe is a human rights and law body set up in 1949, whereas the European Union, an economic and political bloc with shared law, began with the Maastricht Treaty of 1992-93.
2. NATO is a military alliance, and its Article 5 has been invoked once, on 2 October 2011, after the attacks on the United States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Council of Europe is a human rights and law body set up in 1949, and the EU, an economic and political bloc with shared law, began with the Maastricht Treaty of 1992-93. Statement 2 describes NATO rightly and says Article 5 was invoked once after the attacks on the United States, but dates it 2 October 2011; the date was 2 October 2001. The one-digit change tempts because the rest is accurate. Remember: Article 5 was used once, on 2 October 2001.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and Asia-Pacific trade arrangements:
Statement I: India stayed out of RCEP because of its trade deficit with China, weak safeguards against import surges, worry for dairy and farming, and unsettled rules of origin.
Statement II: India signed the goods agreement with ASEAN in 2009 and services and investment agreements in 2014, but it joined three of the four IPEF pillars, stayed out of the trade pillar, and is not a member of APEC or CPTPP.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I. The reasons for staying out of RCEP are the deficit with China, weak safeguards against import surges, worry for dairy and farming, and unsettled rules of origin. Statement II lists true facts: the ASEAN goods agreement of 2009, the services and investment agreements of 2014, IPEF in three of four pillars, and no membership of APEC or CPTPP. These describe India's other trade choices, not its reasons for leaving RCEP. Remember: the reasons belong to RCEP; IPEF, APEC and CPTPP are separate facts.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The India-France strategic partnership began in 1998, and France joined the sanctions imposed after India's nuclear tests.
A tariff cut under the India-EU deal also removes the EU carbon charge, because tariffs and CBAM are one tool.
The G4 is formed by France, Germany, India and Japan, who back each other's bids for permanent Security Council seats.
The G4 is formed by Germany, India, Brazil and Japan, who back each other's bids for permanent Security Council seats.
qs.e: The fourth statement is correct: Germany, India, Brazil and Japan form the G4 and back each other's bids for permanent Security Council seats. The first is half right, since the partnership began in 1998, but France did not join sanctions after India's nuclear tests. The second fails because tariffs and CBAM are separate tools, so a tariff cut does not remove the carbon charge. The third puts France in the G4, which tempts because it is a Security Council member already. Remember: G4 is Germany, India, Brazil, Japan; France stayed out of the sanctions.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Look East and Act East policies:
Statement I: India's Look East Policy began in the early 1990s, after the 1991 reforms, as a drive for trade and investment.
Statement II: India wants markets, maritime security and a land bridge for the North-East through Myanmar, and the Kaladan project runs from Kolkata and Haldia to Sittwe port, up the Kaladan river to Paletwa and then by road to Mizoram.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct, but Statement II does not explain Statement I. Look East began in the early 1990s after the 1991 reforms as a trade and investment drive. Statement II gives India's later wants and the Kaladan route from Kolkata and Haldia by sea to Sittwe, by river to Paletwa and by road to Mizoram. Those aims belong to the Act East stage of 2014, so they describe what followed, not why the first policy began. Remember: Look East began with the 1991 reforms; the land bridge belongs to Act East.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the India-EU trade negotiations:
Statement I: Conclusion of a trade deal is not entry into force, because legal review, Council adoption, signing, Parliament consent and Indian ratification still follow, and the talks relaunched in June 2022 had three tracks: trade, investment protection and geographical indications.
Statement II: In the negotiations India wants lower tariffs on cars and stronger intellectual property rules, while the EU wants easier access for textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals and IT services.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct and Statement II is not. A concluded deal still needs legal review, Council adoption, signing, Parliament consent and Indian ratification, and the 2022 relaunch had three tracks: trade, investment protection and geographical indications. Statement II swaps the demands: India wants easier access for textiles, leather, pharmaceuticals and IT services, and the EU wants lower Indian tariffs on cars and stronger intellectual property rules. The swap tempts because each side's list is plausible for either. Remember: India asks for textiles and services; the EU asks for cars.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indo-Pacific:
1. The Indo-Pacific idea treats the Indian Ocean and the western Pacific as one connected strategic space, while Asia-Pacific is an older term centred on the Pacific rim that often leaves out the Indian Ocean.
2. The Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative was launched on 4 November 2019 at the East Asia Summit in Singapore, and it is open to all.
3. The Strait of Malacca lies between the Malay Peninsula and the Indonesian island of Sumatra and links the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Indo-Pacific joins the Indian Ocean and the western Pacific, unlike the older Asia-Pacific term, and the Strait of Malacca between the Malay Peninsula and Sumatra links the Indian Ocean with the South China Sea. Statement 2 fails on the venue: the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative was launched at the East Asia Summit in Bangkok, not Singapore. Singapore tempts because Modi set out India's vision there in 2018. Remember: the vision was spoken in Singapore, the Initiative launched in Bangkok.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the Hague summit of 25 June 2025 NATO set a goal of 5% of GDP a year by 2035, of which at least 3.5% is for core defence.
2. The Hague goal asks for at least 1.5% of GDP on core defence and up to 3.5% on resilience, with a review in
2029.
3. India ordered 36 Rafale in September 2016 for the Air Force, and agreed on 28 April 2025 to buy 26 Rafale- Marine for the Navy.
4. India's position is that the EU carbon border mechanism is a unilateral trade barrier that ignores common but differentiated responsibilities, while the EU's reasoning is carbon leakage.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. The Hague goal is 5% of GDP by 2035, with at least 3.5% for core defence; the Rafale orders are 36 for the Air Force in 2016 and 26 Rafale-Marine for the Navy agreed on 28 April 2025; and India's stated position on CBAM is that it is a unilateral barrier, while the EU cites carbon leakage. Statement 2 swaps the split: core defence takes at least 3.5% and resilience up to 1.5%. Remember: 3.5 core, 1.5 resilience, reviewed in 2029.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. Australia lies in the southern hemisphere between the Indian and Pacific oceans, and it is a Quad partner of India, with Japan and the United States. India and Australia held their first 2+2 of foreign and defence secretaries on 12 December 2017. The Comprehensive Strategic Partnership came on 4 June 2020, and the ECTA was signed on 2 April 2022 and entered into force on 29 December 2022. In Myanmar a state of emergency was imposed on 1 February 2021 and power passed to the State Administrative Council. India says it deals with the military authorities for security and border reasons while urging dialogue and a return to democracy. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. Australia, a Quad partner of India, lies in the southern hemisphere between the Indian and Pacific oceans.
2. The 2+2 of foreign and defence secretaries came after the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.
3. India's stated approach in Myanmar is to deal with the military authorities for security and border reasons while urging dialogue and a return to democracy.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct, so two conclusions hold and they include statement 1. Australia lies in the southern hemisphere between the two oceans and is a Quad partner, and India's stated approach to the Myanmar authorities pairs security and border dealings with urging dialogue and democracy. Statement 2 reverses the order: the 2+2 of 12 December 2017 came before the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership of 4 June 2020. It tempts because a partnership seems the earlier, broader step. Remember: 2+2 in 2017, partnership in 2020, ECTA signed in 2022.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about West Asia:
1. The Balfour Declaration of 1917 backed a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.
2. In 1956 Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal on 26 July, and Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt.
3. UN General Assembly Resolution 181 of 1947 recommended an Arab state and a Jewish state, with Jerusalem placed under Israeli control.
4. In 1956 India stayed publicly neutral, criticised the use of force and held that the canal should stay under Egyptian ownership.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Balfour Declaration of 1917 backed a national home in Palestine, Nasser nationalised the canal on 26 July 1956 and Israel, Britain and France attacked Egypt, and India stayed publicly neutral, criticised force and wanted the canal to stay under Egyptian ownership. Statement 3 fails on Jerusalem: Resolution 181 recommended an international regime for the city, not Israeli control. It tempts because the resolution did name a Jewish state. Remember: Resolution 181 gave Jerusalem an international regime.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a body or region and a description:
1. BIMSTEC : established on 6 June 1997 in Bangkok, with its secretariat in Dhaka
2. ASEAN : an intergovernmental group with no common court or parliament, unlike the European Union
3. Mainland Southeast Asia : Myanmar, Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Malaysia
4. BIMSTEC : a group of eleven members, with its secretariat in Jakarta Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
qs.e: Pairs 1 and 2 are correctly matched. BIMSTEC was established in Bangkok on 6 June 1997 with a Dhaka secretariat, and ASEAN has no common court or parliament, so it is not an Asian EU. Pair 3 puts Malaysia on the mainland, but Vietnam is the fifth mainland member and Malaysia is in the maritime part. Pair 4 borrows ASEAN's Jakarta secretariat for BIMSTEC, which has seven members. The look-alike names tempt the borrowing. Remember: BIMSTEC has seven members and Dhaka; ASEAN has Jakarta.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the European Union as of 2026:
1. The 16th EU-India Summit in New Delhi on 27 January 2026 concluded negotiations for the India-EU FTA.
2. Trade is a power of the EU bloc, so India negotiates tariffs with Brussels and not with each capital.
3. The Trade and Technology Council, announced in 2022, covers AI, semiconductors and 6G.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: All three statements are correct. Negotiations for the India-EU FTA were concluded at the 16th summit in New Delhi on 27 January 2026, which is not the same as entry into force. Because trade is a power of the bloc, India deals with Brussels on tariffs. The Trade and Technology Council, announced in 2022, covers AI, semiconductors and 6G. Doubt may come from mistaking conclusion for signing, or from thinking member capitals bargain separately. Remember: Brussels negotiates, Delhi hosted the conclusion, and the Council covers technology.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's trade agreements with European partners:
1. EFTA is a free-trade body set up in 1960, and its members are Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Sweden.
2. The EFTA states aim at USD 100 billion of investment in India over fifteen years and one million direct jobs, which is an aim with no penalty if missed.
3. Under the CETA with the United Kingdom, India gets zero duty on about 99% of its exports, and the UK government says 90% of its goods go duty-free or at reduced tariffs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The EFTA investment and jobs figures are an aim with no penalty if missed, and under the CETA India gets zero duty on about 99% of its exports, while the UK government says 90% of its goods go duty-free or at reduced tariffs. Statement 1 swaps a member: EFTA is Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, all outside the EU, and Sweden is an EU state. It tempts because Sweden is a Nordic neighbour of Norway and Iceland. Remember: EFTA has Switzerland, not Sweden; its figures are aims.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about India's defence and economic ties with Russia and the United States is correct?
o: The commission on trade, economy, science, technology and culture, IRIGC-TEC, is co-chaired by India's Defence Minister and Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister.
According to SIPRI data, Russia's share of India's arms imports rose between 2009-13 and 2019-23, from 36 per cent to 76 per cent of the total.
IRIGC-TEC, the commission on trade, economy, science, technology and culture, has India's External Affairs Minister and Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister as its co-chairs.
The MQ-9B drone deal of October 2024 and the understanding to co-produce GE F414 engines for the Tejas Mk2 are both defence agreements between India and Russia.
qs.e: The key is C. IRIGC-TEC is the commission on trade, economy, science, technology and culture, co-chaired by India's External Affairs Minister and Russia's First Deputy Prime Minister. Option A puts the Defence Minister in the chair. Option B reverses the SIPRI trend: that data show Russia's share falling from 76 per cent in 2009-13 to 36 per cent in 2019-23. Option D gives Russia two deals that belong to the United States. Option A tempts because defence is the oldest pillar of the tie. Remember: IRIGC-TEC pairs the External Affairs Minister with the First Deputy Prime Minister.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements: I. In 2017 Chinese crews began extending a road on the Doklam plateau on 16 June, about 270 Indian troops moved in to stop them, and the standoff ended with a mutual disengagement on 28 August. II. Doklam lies at the meeting point of India, Bhutan and China, close to the Chumbi valley of Tibet, and the Jampheri ridge there points toward the Siliguri Corridor. III. As of 2025 about 3,232.218 km of the India-Bangladesh border was fenced, leaving a gap of 864.482 km. Consider the following claims about how the statements given above are related:
1. Statement 3 shows that the unfenced gap is longer than the fenced stretch, so that less than half of the border with Bangladesh was fenced as of 2025.
2. Statement 2 helps explain why India reads a Chinese road near Doklam as a security matter, even though, in Indian commerce data as reported, China passed the United States in 2025-26 as India's largest trading partner.
3. India's stated objection to the Belt and Road, that the Pakistan corridor runs through territory India claims, is an objection about one route, and India's position on the road in Statement 1, that it changed the status quo against a 2012 understanding, is likewise about one stretch of land.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Claims 2 and 3 are correct. Doklam sits at the meeting point of India, Bhutan and China, and its Jampheri ridge points toward the Siliguri Corridor, so a Chinese road there is a security matter whatever the trade figures. India's Belt and Road objection and its Doklam position both concern a specific route or stretch of land. Claim 1 reverses the fencing figures: about 3,232.218 km was fenced and 864.482 km was the gap. It tempts because a gap of that size sounds large. Remember: fenced 3,232, gap 864; Doklam road from 16 June to 28 August.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements: I. Mohamed Muizzu went to China in January 2024 on a state visit before any visit to India, breaking the practice of going to India first. II. Indian military personnel in the Maldives flew a Dornier aircraft and helicopters that India had given for search and rescue, and civilian technicians replaced them by 10 May 2024. III. Delft Island (Neduntheevu) is the biggest of seven inhabited islands in the Palk Strait. Consider the following claims about how the statements given above are related:
1. Statement 2 shows a step on the question of Indian military personnel, which Muizzu's India Out campaign had opposed.
2. Statement 3 describes an island of the Maldives that lies near Minicoy, which links it to the first two statements.
3. Statement 1 shows a break with the India First policy that his predecessor Solih had followed.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Claims 1 and 3 are correct. The replacement of the Indian personnel by civilian technicians by 10 May 2024 answered the India Out campaign against them, and the January 2024 visit to China broke the India First practice of Solih. Claim 2 misplaces Delft Island, which is the biggest of seven inhabited islands in the Palk Strait and has no link with Minicoy or the Maldives. It tempts because all three statements are island stories of the Indian Ocean. Remember: Delft in the Palk Strait; Minicoy faces the Maldives.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's neighbourhood and its trade partners in Europe:
1. ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus of April 2021 asks for an end to violence in Myanmar.
2. Gorkha refers to soldiers from the hills of Nepal who serve in the Indian Army under a 1947 tripartite agreement among Britain, India and Nepal that divided the Gorkha regiments.
3. India's position is that it supports free, fair and inclusive elections in Myanmar and engages those who hold power on border and projects.
4. The India-EFTA TEPA was signed on 10 March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025, while the UK CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: All four statements are correct, so only the full set fits. ASEAN's Five-Point Consensus of April 2021 asks for an end to violence in Myanmar. Gorkhas serve under the tripartite agreement of 1947 among Britain, India and Nepal. India states its own position on the Myanmar election and does not thereby recognise the military government. The two European deals differ in dates, and the lure is to swap them. Remember: TEPA signed 10 March 2024, in force 1 October 2025; CETA signed 24 July 2025, in force 15 July 2026.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. Three bodies work from European cities. The first sits at Strasbourg, was set up in 1949 and runs the European Convention on Human Rights with its own court. The second is a treaty alliance whose core tool is Article 5, and Sweden became its 32nd member on 7 March 2024. The third has a single market, shared law and the euro, and four of its members stay outside the second. Russia has been at war with Ukraine since February 2022. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The first body is a human rights and law body, the second is a military alliance and the third is an economic and political bloc with shared law.
2. Austria and Poland are both among the twenty-three states that belong to the second body and the third body.
3. Russia ceased to be a member of the first body on 16 March 2023.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only conclusion 1 is correct. The Council of Europe, set up in 1949 and seated at Strasbourg, is the human rights and law body; NATO is the military alliance; the EU is the economic and political bloc with shared law. Conclusion 2 fails on Austria, one of the four EU states outside NATO, although Poland is among the twenty-three states in both. Conclusion 3 shifts the year: Russia ceased to be a member of the Council of Europe on 16 March 2022. Remember: Strasbourg means rights; Austria is EU only; Russia left in 2022.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the United States:
1. The framework announced in February 2026 is a signed treaty, under which India is bound to buy 500 billion US dollars of US goods over five years.
2. The Generalized System of Preferences gives developing countries duty-free entry for some goods, India stays on the US Priority Watch List for intellectual property rights, and Indian material says that iCET, which began on 31 January 2023, continues as TRUST, which came in February 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. The framework of February 2026 is not a signed treaty, and India stated an intent, an aim and not a binding duty, to buy 500 billion US dollars of US goods over five years; statement 1 turns intent into duty. In statement 2, the Generalized System of Preferences gives duty-free entry for some goods, India stays on the Priority Watch List for intellectual property rights, and Indian material says iCET continues as TRUST. The lure is that a framework sounds like a treaty. Remember: framework, not treaty; intent, not duty.

qs.q:
The figure given below shows two points at which the Kali river may be said to begin. Consider the following observations about Nepal and its boundary with India: I. India's position is that the Kali begins where streams from the Kalapani springs join the Lipu Gad, while Nepal's position is that it begins in the Kuthi Yankti further west, so that the area east of it is Nepali. II. Nepal is landlocked; it touches India on its east, south and west and Tibet (China) on its north, and five Indian states lie along the border: Sikkim, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand. III. On 8 May 2020 India opened an 80 km Dharchula-Lipulekh road that Nepal said crosses its land, and on 20 May 2020 Nepal released a new map showing Kalapani, Limpiyadhura and Lipulekh as Nepali. Consider the following inferences from the observations given above:
1. In the figure, the shaded area lies on Nepal's side if the Kali is taken to begin at the point marked A, and on India's side if it is taken to begin at the point marked B.
2. Nepal's new map of 20 May 2020 came before India opened the Dharchula-Lipulekh road.
3. The five Indian states named lie along the east, south and west of Nepal, while Tibet (China) lies on its north.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
qs.e: Inferences 1 and 3 can be drawn. In the figure, A lies on the Kuthi Yankti, where Nepal says the Kali begins, further west than B, where India says it begins; a start at A puts the shaded area east of the river, on Nepal's side. The five Indian states lie along the east, south and west, with Tibet on the north. Inference 2 reverses the dates: the road came on 8 May and the map on 20 May 2020. It tempts because Nepal's claim goes back to 1817. Remember: road on 8 May, map on 20 May; a start further west gives Nepal more land.

qs.q: The figure given below shows two routes between India and Russia, with three parts of one corridor marked A, B and C. Which one of the following statements is correct?
o: Soviet help built the steel plants at Bhilai and Bokaro after Nehru visited Moscow and Khrushchev visited India in 1965.
CAATSA, which became US law in 2017, was applied to India in December 2020 over the S-400, for which India had signed in 2018.
The corridor in the figure runs through the country marked A, which is Türkiye, to the Black Sea marked B, and on to Russia.
The corridor in the figure runs by ship, rail and road through the country marked A, which is Iran, and the sea marked B is the Caspian Sea.
qs.e: The key is D. The International North-South Transport Corridor runs by ship, rail and road through Iran to Russia, and the sea it crosses is the Caspian Sea. Option C names Türkiye and the Black Sea, which are not on the route. Option B gives CAATSA to India, but the US applied it to Türkiye in December 2020 over the S-400. Option A shifts the year: Nehru visited Moscow and Khrushchev visited India in 1955. Remember: INSTC goes through Iran to the Caspian; CAATSA fell on Türkiye.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about India and the Indian Ocean is correct?
o: India's position is that it is a resident power and a net security provider, meaning a state that keeps the trade of the ocean for itself.
About 90 to 95 per cent of India's trade by volume moves by sea.
A tracking terminal for India's human spaceflight is planned on the Hallaniyat (Kuria Muria) Islands off Oman.
Project Mausam is India's plan to build a chain of naval bases on islands across the ocean.
qs.e: The key is B: about 90 to 95 per cent of India's trade by volume moves by sea. Option A changes the meaning of net security provider, which is a state that helps keep the ocean safe for others; that is India's own stated aim. Option C moves the planned tracking terminal from the Cocos (Keeling) Islands to the Hallaniyat Islands. Option D mistakes Project Mausam, a plan to revive cultural ties across the ocean, for a base plan. Remember: the sea carries 90 to 95 per cent; Mausam is culture, not bases.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Ocean and its islands:
1. India's Ministry of External Affairs dates the Maritime Boundary Treaty, which settled the Maldives' claim to Minicoy, to 1979.
2. Over 60 per cent of the world's oil shipments cross the Indian Ocean, which is ringed by more than 40 littoral states, meaning states with a coast on it.
3. The Hallaniyat (Kuria Muria) Islands are five islands off south-east Oman on the Arabian Sea, of which only Al-Hallaniyah is inhabited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Over 60 per cent of the world's oil shipments cross the Indian Ocean, which more than 40 littoral states ring, and the Hallaniyat Islands are five islands off south-east Oman of which only Al-Hallaniyah is inhabited. Statement 1 takes the date from the weaker account: India's Ministry of External Affairs says 1976, though one account says 1979. It tempts because the 1979 figure is printed beside the official one. Remember: use the Ministry's 1976 for the Minicoy treaty.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about the western Indian Ocean and Europe:
1. Mayotte became France's 101st department on 31 March 2011, and IORA lists France as a member in respect of Mayotte.
2. Mayotte stayed with France in the votes of 1974 and 1976, and a 1976 draft Security Council resolution backing Comoros, an IORA member made of Grande Comore, Anjouan and Moheli, was vetoed by the United Kingdom.
3. Assumption Island, which covers about 11.6 square km, lies in the Aldabra group about 1,135 km north-east of Victoria.
4. France, which holds Reunion and Mayotte, belongs to both the EU and NATO, and NATO is the military arm of the EU.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: None of the statements is correct. IORA lists France as a member in respect of Reunion, not Mayotte, though Mayotte did become the 101st department on 31 March 2011. It was France that vetoed the 1976 draft resolution backing Comoros. Assumption Island lies south-west of Victoria, not north-east. NATO is not the military arm of the EU: it has members outside the EU and four EU states stay outside it. Each lure keeps a true name beside a wrong detail. Remember: Reunion carries France's IORA seat; France vetoed in 1976.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's links with its South Asian neighbours:
1. India may use the Chattogram and Mongla ports of Bangladesh for cargo bound for the North East.
2. An enclave is a country with no sea coast, so it needs a neighbour's ports and roads.
3. Under SAFTA India gives duty-free, quota-free access to nearly all Bangladeshi products.
4. Mitra Shakti is the annual India-Sri Lanka navy exercise and SLINEX the annual army exercise.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only two statements are correct: 1 and 3. India may use Chattogram and Mongla for North East cargo, and under SAFTA it gives duty-free, quota-free access to nearly all Bangladeshi products. Statement 2 gives the meaning of a landlocked state, not an enclave, which is a piece of one country completely surrounded by another. Statement 4 swaps the services: Mitra Shakti is the army exercise and SLINEX the navy one. Each lure uses a real term from the same set of ideas. Remember: enclave means surrounded; landlocked means no coast; Mitra army, SLINEX navy.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and Bangladesh:
1. The land boundary is about 4,096.7 km long and runs along five Indian states: West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.
2. The Siliguri Corridor joins the North East to the rest of India and is about 22 km wide at its narrowest.
3. The Farakka Barrage, about 18 km from the Bangladesh border, stands on the Teesta in Murshidabad district and sends part of the flow into the Hooghly to keep the Kolkata port usable.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Two statements are correct: 1 and 2. The land boundary of about 4,096.7 km runs along West Bengal, Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, and the Siliguri Corridor, about 22 km wide at its narrowest, joins the North East to the rest of India. Statement 3 names the wrong river: the Farakka Barrage stands on the Ganga and sends part of its flow into the Hooghly. It tempts because the Teesta is the other river in the news. Remember: Farakka means Ganga; Teesta has no treaty.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's ties with Europe:
1. The Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism makes the price of imports reflect their embedded carbon emissions, so as to stop carbon leakage, which means firms moving output to places with stricter carbon rules.
2. Talks on the Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement between India and the EU opened in Brussels on 28 June 2007 and stalled in 2013, the last round being held in New Delhi on 13 May 2013.
3. Moldova is an EU candidate country between Romania and Ukraine.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. The Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement talks opened in Brussels on 28 June 2007 and stalled after the last round in New Delhi on 13 May 2013, and Moldova is an EU candidate country between Romania and Ukraine. Statement 1 turns the purpose around: carbon leakage means firms moving output to places with weaker, not stricter, carbon rules. It tempts because strict rules sound like the thing a border charge protects. Remember: CBAM stops flight to weaker rules.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the western Indian Ocean:
Statement I: A joint military facility on Assumption Island was agreed in 2015, but a revised pact was rejected by the National Assembly of Seychelles in 2018 after protests that the islands should stay out of the India- China rivalry, which shows that India's access depends on local politics and that ownership is not on offer.
Statement II: As of 2026 India chairs IORA, which is a navy forum, and its other links in the western ocean include the IMT TRILAT naval exercise with Mozambique and Tanzania, first held in 2022, and Operation Vanilla, its flood relief to Madagascar in January 2020.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct and Statement II is not. The facility agreed in 2015 lost its revised pact in 2018 when Seychelles' National Assembly rejected it, a limit of Indian strategy: access depends on local politics and ownership is not on offer. Statement II fails on the type of body: IORA is a forum of governments, while IONS is the navy forum. The 2022 exercise and the January 2020 relief are correct. It tempts because India leads both bodies in 2026. Remember: IORA governments, IONS navies.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a place and a fact about it:
1. Chagos Archipelago : India's position is firm support for Mauritius, in line with the 2019 General Assembly resolution
2. Agalega : a dependency of Mauritius with two outer islands about 1,050 km north of the main island
3. Agalega airstrip and jetty : jointly inaugurated by Modi and the Mauritian Prime Minister in February 2025
4. Chagos Archipelago : India's position, reiterated in March 2025, is neutrality between Mauritius and the United Kingdom
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Two pairs are correctly matched: the first and the second. India's position on Chagos is firm support for Mauritius, in line with the 2019 General Assembly resolution, and Agalega is a dependency of Mauritius with two outer islands about 1,050 km north of the main island. The third pair moves the inauguration of the airstrip and jetty to 2025; it was February 2024. The fourth swaps firm support for neutrality. The date lure borrows the year of the March 2025 reiteration. Remember: Agalega airstrip, February 2024; Chagos, support for Mauritius.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and China:
1. On 15 June 2020 a clash in the Galwan Valley killed 20 Indian soldiers, the first deaths on the border in decades, and in February 2021 China said four of its soldiers died.
2. Doklam is a plateau near the point where the boundaries of India, Bhutan and China meet.
3. On 4 April 2025 China placed seven heavy rare earths and related products under export licensing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: All three statements are correct. The clash in the Galwan Valley on 15 June 2020 killed 20 Indian soldiers, the first deaths on the border in decades, and China said in February 2021 that four of its soldiers died. Doklam is a plateau near the point where the India, Bhutan and China boundaries meet. On 4 April 2025 China put seven heavy rare earths and related products under export licensing. No word is changed in any of them, so no shorter code fits. Remember: Galwan 15 June 2020, twenty killed; rare earths 4 April 2025.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. India's treaty with Nepal is the base of a border that people cross with little or no checking, and its revised treaty with Bhutan was signed in 2007. In Dhaka, student-led protests in August 2024 led to Sheikh Hasina leaving for India. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The 2007 text with Bhutan kept the duty to be guided by India's advice, which the 1950 text with Nepal dropped.
2. Muhammad Yunus took the oath on 5 August 2024, and Sheikh Hasina left for India on 8 August.
3. The Treaty of Peace and Friendship with Nepal was signed in New Delhi on 31 July 1950.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: No conclusion is correct. The 2007 treaty with Bhutan dropped the duty to be guided by India's advice, and Nepal's 1950 text never carried it. Hasina left for India on 5 August 2024 and Yunus took the oath on 8 August. The Treaty of Peace and Friendship was signed in Kathmandu on 31 July 1950, not in New Delhi. Each lure swaps one detail of a look-alike pair: Bhutan against Nepal, departure against oath, Kathmandu against Delhi. Remember: Bhutan 2007 dropped the advice duty; Nepal 1950 never had it; Kathmandu, 31 July.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about European groupings:
1. The North Atlantic Treaty was signed in Washington on 4 April 1949 by 12 countries, among them Canada and the United States.
2. The Normandy Format, which began in June 2014 for peace talks on eastern Ukraine, brought together France, Germany, Poland and Ukraine.
3. As of 2026 the EU has 32 members and NATO has 27, and the two lists overlap a great deal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. NATO's founding treaty was signed in Washington on 4 April 1949 by 12 countries, including Canada and the United States. Statement 2 puts Poland in the Normandy Format in place of Russia; Poland belongs to the Weimar Triangle with France and Germany. Statement 3 swaps the sizes: as of 2026 the EU has 27 members and NATO has 32. The lures borrow real members and real numbers from the same pages. Remember: Normandy has Russia; Weimar has Poland; EU 27, NATO 32.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and Sri Lanka:
1. India seeks a stable island, safe sea lanes, limits on Chinese military use of ports and a negotiated settlement of the ethnic issue within a united Sri Lanka, while Sri Lanka wants recovery, debt relief, investment, trade access and ties with both India and China.
2. Anura Kumara Dissanayake, whose alliance is built around the leftist JVP, made China his first overseas trip as President, on a state visit in December 2024, and the 2022 crisis came from slow causes that included war and borrowing, weak exports and the Easter bombings of 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 1 is correct. India's wants and Sri Lanka's wants are as listed: a stable island, safe sea lanes, limits on Chinese military use of ports and a settlement within a united Sri Lanka; recovery, debt relief, investment, trade access and ties with both India and China. Statement 2 fails on the destination: Dissanayake made India his first overseas trip as President, on a state visit from 15 to 17 December 2024. The causes of 2022 are right. China tempts because Sri Lanka balances both powers. Remember: first trip to India, 15 to 17 December 2024.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's land boundary with Bangladesh and its neighbours:
1. The 100th Amendment, dated 7 May 2015, let India give land away; ratification papers were exchanged on 6 June, and the land itself changed hands on 31 July-1 August 2015.
2. Among Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh and Myanmar, Bangladesh and Myanmar are the landlocked states, which have no sea coast and need a neighbour's ports and roads.
3. The 2015 agreement drew a brand new border, since the agreement of 1974 had left the whole line open.
How many of the above statements are correct?
qs.e: Only one statement is correct: statement 1. The 100th Amendment of 7 May 2015 let India give land away, ratification papers followed on 6 June, and the land changed hands on 31 July-1 August. Statement 2 names the wrong pair: Nepal and Bhutan are landlocked, while Bangladesh and Myanmar have coasts. Statement 3 is the common wrong idea: the 1974 agreement set most of the line and the 2011 Protocol fixed the rest, so 2015 completed an older settlement. Remember: landlocked means Nepal and Bhutan; 2015 completed, not created.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement I: The 50 per cent tariff on Indian goods in August 2025 included an extra 25 per cent duty over Russian oil, which ended when statements of 6-7 February 2026 set a framework for an Interim Agreement at 18 per cent.
Statement II: The tariff of 50 per cent in August 2025 was made up of a 25 per cent reciprocal tariff plus a further 25 per cent over Russian oil.
Statement III: A Section 301 forced-labour action put 10 per cent on most Indian goods from 24 February 2026, and a 10 per cent global surcharge under Section 122 followed it from 24 July 2026.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement II and Statement III are correct and both of them explain Statement I
Both Statement II and Statement III are correct, but only one of them explains Statement I
Only one of the Statements II and III is correct and that explains Statement I
Neither Statement II nor Statement III is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct, and only Statement II of the two that follow is correct and it explains Statement I. The 50 per cent of August 2025 was a 25 per cent reciprocal tariff plus 25 per cent over Russian oil, so when the Russian-oil duty ended after the framework of 6-7 February 2026, the extra 25 per cent went. Statement III reverses the order: the Section 122 surcharge ran from 24 February to 24 July 2026 and the Section 301 action followed. Both are 10 per cent measures of 2026, which tempts the swap. Remember: 25 plus 25 made 50; Section 122 first, Section 301 after.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. Sri Lanka's reserves fell to about US$2.36 billion by January 2022, and the country then defaulted. India, acting as first responder, stood by its neighbour. India and Sri Lanka have a trade agreement that was signed in December 1998. Seychelles, another island state of the same ocean, balances its ties with India and China. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. Sri Lanka defaulted in April 2022, and President Gotabaya Rajapaksa was forced out in mid-July 2022 after mass protests.
2. The Indian Peace Keeping Force landed in Sri Lanka after the Accord signed on 29 July 1987, and Seychelles takes part in the Colombo Security Conclave but is not an IORA member.
3. A free trade agreement goes further than a CEPA, since a CEPA only cuts tariffs and leaves each side's other rules in place.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
There is only one correct statement.
qs.e: Only conclusion 1 is correct. Sri Lanka defaulted in April 2022 and President Gotabaya Rajapaksa was forced out in mid-July 2022 after mass protests. Conclusion 2 fails on IORA: Seychelles is a member of IORA as well as a participant in the Colombo Security Conclave, though the Accord date and the IPKF landing are right. Conclusion 3 reverses the pair: an FTA cuts tariffs and leaves other rules in place, and CEPAs go further. Both are trade acronyms, which tempts the swap. Remember: default in April, exit in July 2022; FTA narrow, CEPA wide.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the United States:
1. The United States calls India a non-NATO ally, a label for close defence work, and India says it will not join a military alliance.
2. GSOMIA, signed in 2002, protects classified military information either side shares and also shares technology on its own, and the ten-year defence framework was signed at Kuala Lumpur by Rajnath Singh and Pete Hegseth on 31 October 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Neither statement is correct. The United States calls India a Major Defense Partner, which is a label for close defence work and not a treaty of alliance, and India says it will not join a military alliance. GSOMIA, signed in 2002, protects classified military information either side shares but does not share technology on its own. The Kuala Lumpur framework of 31 October 2025 is right, which tempts a reader to accept the whole sentence. Remember: Major Defense Partner, not ally; GSOMIA guards secrets, not technology.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about India and China is correct?
o: India gives the length of its boundary with China as about 4,096.7 km, running along Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
India gives the length of its boundary with China as about 3,488 km, running along Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh.
Ambassadors returned in 1981 and boundary talks began in 1976, and Rajiv Gandhi's visit in December 1988 formed a joint working group.
The Line of Actual Control is an international boundary fixed by treaty and marked on the ground along most of the frontier.
qs.e: The key is B. India gives the length as about 3,488 km, along Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh. Option A gives 4,096.7 km, which is the length of the Bangladesh border. Option C swaps the years: ambassadors returned in 1976 and boundary talks began in 1981. Option D confuses the Line of Actual Control, the line each side holds in practice and not drawn on an agreed map, with an international boundary. Option A tempts because 4,096.7 km is a well-known border figure. Remember: 3,488 km, with Ladakh; 1976 ambassadors, 1981 talks.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's dealings with Bhutan and Myanmar:
1. After a magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck Myanmar on 28 March 2025, India began Operation Brahma that same day and, by 9 April, had delivered over 656 tonnes of aid and flown in an 80-member NDRF team.
2. Among the five hydropower plants that India developed jointly with Bhutan, Chukha is the smallest at 60 MW, and the five together total 3,156 MW.
3. Kyaukphyu, a deep-water port on the Rakhine coast built with Chinese backing, is part of a China-Myanmar economic corridor, and Indian writing often describes India's Sittwe port as a counter to it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Operation Brahma began on the day of the 28 March 2025 earthquake, with over 656 tonnes of aid by 9 April and an 80-member NDRF team. Kyaukphyu is a Chinese-backed port that Indian writing sets against Sittwe. Statement 2 fails on the plant: Kurichhu is the 60 MW project and Chukha is 336 MW. It tempts because the total of 3,156 MW and the five names are right. Remember: Kurichhu 60 MW is the smallest; Tala and Punatsangchhu-II, 1,020 MW each, the largest.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's response to China after the Galwan clash:
Statement I: After Galwan, India banned many Chinese mobile apps from 2020 and tightened screening of Chinese investment under Press Note 3 of 2020, which needs prior approval for investment from countries that share a land border with India.
Statement II: Because border trade restarted through Nathu La, Shipki La and Lipulekh on 1 August 2026, the dispute over Aksai Chin, about 38,000 sq km under Chinese control but claimed by India as part of Ladakh, is now settled.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Statement I is correct and Statement II is not. After Galwan India banned many Chinese apps from 2020 and screened investment under Press Note 3 of 2020, which needs prior approval from countries sharing a land border. Statement II has true facts, since trade reopened on 1 August 2026 and Aksai Chin stays under Chinese control, but the conclusion overreaches: reopened trade posts do not settle the line. It tempts because a calmer border looks like a settled one. Remember: trade reopens, the line stays open.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about Bhutan is correct?
o: Gelephu Mindfulness City, announced by the King of Bhutan on 17 December 2023, covers about 2,500 sq km on the Indian border as a special administrative region.
The revised treaty signed on 8 February 2007 kept the duty of Bhutan to be guided by India's advice on external relations.
The Kokrajhar-Gelephu and Banarhat-Samtse rail lines, covered by a memorandum of 29 September 2025, are working lines that cost Rs 4,033.34 crore.
Gelephu Mindfulness City, announced on 17 December 2023, is an ordinary part of Bhutan's districts and follows the normal laws of the country.
qs.e: The first statement is correct: the King of Bhutan announced Gelephu Mindfulness City on 17 December 2023, a special administrative region of about 2,500 sq km on the Indian border. The 2007 treaty dropped the duty to be guided by India's advice, so the second fails. The two rail lines are planned, and Rs 4,033.34 crore is an estimate, so the third fails. The fourth fails because the city has its own legal framework. It tempts because the 2007 treaty still keeps close consultation. Remember: Gelephu has its own laws; the rail lines are only planned.

qs.q:
Read the following passage. India makes the T-90S tank and the Su-30MKI fighter under licence from Russia, developed the BrahMos missile jointly with Russia, and bought the S-400 air defence system outright. A pact signed in 2025 sets procedures for sending units, warships and aircraft to each other's territory and for logistics in joint exercises. In function it is Russia's counterpart of LEMOA, which covers fuel, supplies and services for exercises, training and relief and does not create bases. Among the frictions in the tie, Russia lifted its arms embargo on Pakistan in 2014, and Russia sees the Quad as a containment tool. On the basis of this passage, consider the following conclusions:
1. The pact of 2025, like LEMOA, supports logistics for the forces of the two countries without creating bases.
2. India bought both the BrahMos and the S-400 from Russia without any joint work on them.
3. Russia's arms embargo decision of 2014 on Pakistan and its view of the Quad are strains in a tie that is otherwise close in defence.
Which one of the following conclusions, based on the above statements, is correct?
o: There is only one correct statement.
There are two correct statements that include statement 1.
qs.e: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Russia's pact of 2025 is the counterpart of LEMOA in function: it covers logistics and movement of forces and is not a basing pact. The 2014 embargo decision on Pakistan and Russia's view of the Quad are listed as frictions. Statement 2 fails because BrahMos was developed jointly, and only the S- 400 was bought outright. It tempts because both are high-value Russian systems. Remember: BrahMos is built together; the S-400 is simply bought.

qs.q: Which one of the following statements about the 1954 agreement on the Tibet region and the frontier with China is correct?
o: Panchsheel is the set of five principles in the preamble of the 1954 agreement, among them non- aggression, non-interference and peaceful coexistence.
Panchsheel was a treaty of friendship between India and China, and the five principles were set out in its main articles.
The middle sector of the frontier, in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand, is the longest of the three sectors at about 1,597 km.
The preamble of the 1954 agreement named five principles, among them mutual defence and a joint commission for the boundary.
qs.e: The first statement is correct: Panchsheel is the set of five principles in the preamble of the 1954 agreement, which dealt with trade and travel in the Tibet region. The second repeats the wrong idea of a friendship pact. The third fails on the length: the western sector in Ladakh is about 1,597 km and the middle sector about 545 km. The fourth invents two principles. The second tempts because Panchsheel later guided India's foreign policy. Remember: Panchsheel is five principles in a preamble, not a friendship pact.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a matter and its description:
1. Second step of the three-step roadmap of China and Bhutan : marking the line on the ground
2. The Motor Vehicles Agreement of 2015 in the BBIN group : signed by Bhutan but not ratified, as of 2026
3. The Doklam road of 2017 : Bhutan protested that it lay in disputed land, while India's position was that it changed the status quo against a 2012 understanding
4. The water ministry MoU of 23 October 2013 : China to provide Brahmaputra flood-season data from 15 May to 15 October each year from 2014
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Three pairs are correctly matched. The roadmap runs from drawing the line on maps, to a joint survey, to marking it on the ground, so marking is the third step and not the second. Bhutan signed the BBIN motor vehicles pact of 2015 but has not ratified it. Bhutan protested the Doklam road and India argued it upset a 2012 understanding. The MoU of 23 October 2013 covers Brahmaputra data from 15 May to 15 October. The first pair tempts because marking is the end result. Remember: maps, then survey, then marking.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India's economic and diplomatic ties with Russia:
Statement I: Settling trade between India and Russia in national currencies fell short of hopes, although Russia supports India's permanent seat in a reformed Security Council and its NSG membership and has not backed Security Council moves against India on Kashmir.
Statement II: Russia piled up rupees in 2023 that it could not easily spend, because the gap in the record trade of
68.7 billion US dollars in 2024-25 favours Russia, with Indian imports of 63.8 billion against exports of 4.9 billion, and settlement in national currencies works only if each side has goods to buy.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II explains Statement I
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct and Statement II does not explain Statement I
Statement I is correct but Statement II is not correct
Statement I is not correct but Statement II is correct
qs.e: Both statements are correct and Statement II explains Statement I. Rupee settlement falls short when one side cannot spend what it earns: Russia piled up rupees in 2023, and with imports of 63.8 billion dollars against exports of 4.9 billion in 2024-25 the gap favours Russia, so it has few Indian goods to buy. Sanctions limiting SWIFT use added to the problem. Russia's diplomatic support at the UN is correct but is a separate matter, and it tempts a reading that good politics means good payments. Remember: national currencies work only when both sides have goods to buy.

qs.q:
Consider the following pairs of a European body or group and its description:
1. Council of the European Union : a meeting of national ministers that discusses, amends and adopts laws, seated in Brussels
2. European Council : a meeting of heads of state or government that sets political direction, mostly by consensus
3. The European Union as of 2026 : 28 member states, with Croatia (2013) the newest
4. Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania : the Baltic states, which appear in India's policy because of their security position next to Russia
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
qs.e: Three pairs are correctly matched. The Council of the European Union is the meeting of national ministers that adopts laws in Brussels, while the European Council is the meeting of heads of state or government. The Baltic states matter to India for their security position next to Russia. The third pair fails on the number: as of 2026 the Union has 27 members, with Croatia, which joined in 2013, the newest. It tempts because the United Kingdom once belonged. Remember: ministers adopt laws; leaders set direction; 27 members in 2026.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Muizzu won the runoff on 30 September 2023 and took office on 17 November 2023 on an India Out campaign that replaced the India First policy of his predecessor Solih, and this meant that the Maldives left India for China for good.
2. Madagascar, the large island off south-east Africa that faces the Mozambique Channel, is a member of the Indian Ocean Rim Association, and the Indian Navy runs a coastal surveillance radar there.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
qs.e: Only statement 2 is correct. Madagascar faces the Mozambique Channel, belongs to IORA and hosts an Indian Navy coastal surveillance radar. In statement 1 the dates and the two policies are right, since Solih followed India First and Muizzu ran on India Out, but the conclusion fails: within a year the Maldives signed a swap and a partnership with India. It tempts because Muizzu went to China first. Remember: small states hedge, so India Out did not mean leaving India for good.

qs.q:
Consider the following statements about India and Europe:
1. The Nordic-Baltic Eight is formed by the five Nordic states together with Estonia, Latvia and Poland.
2. The India-EFTA Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement was signed in New Delhi on 10 March 2024 and entered into force on 1 October 2025.
